docs.title: Approved principles
docs.text:
• Registration, licensing and capacity validation are separate states.
  • Commercial rights are central entitlements; executable permissions are device-bound signed grants.
  • Customer rights may be pooled and reallocated, while grants remain device-bound.
  • The same trust model supports online, assisted-offline and fully air-gapped operation.
  • Marketplace and OTA live inside LMS because they use the same customer, device, entitlement, capacity and release data.
  • Automatic updates consume Stable releases by default; LTS is explicitly controlled by the company.
  • Model files are independently versioned, encrypted, signed, inventory-aware and rollback-capable.
  • Capacity assessment recommends feasible deployment and never silently reduces purchased rights.

docs.title: Architecture Decision Records
docs.text: ADRs document durable architecture decisions, the problem that forced each decision, alternatives rejected, consequences, security/operational impact and follow-up work. They are not one-line summaries and they are not substitutes for requirements.

docs.title: ADR status meanings
docs.text:
Proposed — candidate decision under review; implementation should not rely on it as immutable baseline yet.

Approved — normative architecture baseline. Changes require a superseding ADR or explicit amendment process.

Open Decision — problem/constraints are known but the final choice is intentionally unresolved. Implementation must preserve the documented abstraction.

Deprecated / Superseded — retained for history; a newer ADR is authoritative.

docs.title: When an ADR is required
docs.text:
Create or supersede an ADR when a change materially affects: - trust boundary or cryptographic design - authentication/authorization model - core licensing semantics - deployment topology/codebase strategy - persistence/storage architecture - public/local API compatibility strategy - update/package format or rollback model - offline trust protocol - major module decomposition or cross-module consistency model - telemetry/operational source-of-truth architecture

A normal implementation detail, bug fix or UI copy change does not require an ADR unless it changes one of those durable decisions.

docs.title: Required ADR content
docs.text:
# ADR-XXX — Title

Status: Proposed | Approved | Open Decision | Superseded
Decision class: <domain>
Date: YYYY-MM-DD

## Context
Why the decision is needed; forces/constraints.

## Decision
Normative choice and boundaries.

## Alternatives considered
Serious alternatives and why they were rejected/deferred.

## Consequences
Positive outcomes, costs, risks and migration implications.

## Security / operational impact
Where relevant.

## Related requirements
SDR IDs and handbook sections.

## Follow-up / decision deadline
Implementation work or unresolved choices.

docs.title: Supersession rule
docs.text:
Approved ADRs are historical records. Do not silently rewrite their fundamental decision after implementation. If the architecture changes materially, create a new ADR that states Supersedes: ADR-XXX, update this index, and preserve the old record.

Clarifying detail may be added to an existing ADR only when it does not reverse or materially change the approved decision.

docs.title: Traceability
docs.text: Every approved ADR should map to relevant SDR requirements, implementation epics/issues and verification evidence. SDR states what the system SHALL do; ADR states why this architecture was chosen.

docs.title: ADR-001 — Digitally Signed Device-Bound Grants
docs.text: Status: Approved Decision class: Security / Licensing Scope: Central LMS + Edge License Agent

docs.title: Context
docs.text: LMS must authorize feature execution on connected, intermittently connected and fully air-gapped devices. A central database lookup alone cannot authorize offline runtime, and reusable license files would be vulnerable to copying between devices.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Use centrally issued, digitally signed, device-bound grants as the executable authorization artifact.

A grant SHALL include subject identity, capability/limits, commercial validity, offline/grace policy, revision/supersession, dependencies and signing metadata. The device verifies the grant using a trusted public key before runtime use.

Production signing private keys remain outside normal LMS application/database storage.

docs.title: Central online lookup only
docs.text: Rejected because air-gapped/offline operation is a first-class requirement.

docs.title: Unsigned local license files
docs.text: Rejected because tampering cannot be reliably detected.

docs.title: Customer-wide reusable license key/file
docs.text: Rejected because it increases cloning/reuse risk and weakens device-level allocation/revocation.

docs.title: Positive
docs.text:
• offline verification works without central connectivity
  • tampering/forgery is detectable
  • device-specific quantities and dependencies can be enforced
  • supersession/revision supports controlled renewal/reallocation

docs.title: Negative / cost
docs.text:
• key custody, rotation and trust-store management are required
  • offline revocation is delayed until import/expiry
  • compromised root access on the edge remains outside full software control

docs.title: Security / operational impact
docs.text:
• grant verification fails closed
  • devices persist highest accepted revision
  • signing outage blocks new issuance but not already-valid grants
  • support must distinguish issued, delivered and accepted states

docs.title: Related requirements
docs.text: SDR-LIC-004, SDR-LIC-007, SDR-LIC-008, SDR-SEC-003, SDR-SEC-004

docs.title: Follow-up
docs.text: Grant canonicalization and exact wire format are finalized in implementation/OpenAPI/schema work without changing this decision.

docs.title: ADR-002 — Modular Monolith First
docs.text: Status: Approved Decision class: Backend Architecture

docs.title: Context
docs.text: LMS spans registry, licensing, policy, capacity, marketplace, release, offline workflows, renewals, integrations and audit. Early microservice decomposition would add distributed transactions, deployment overhead and operational complexity before scale boundaries are proven.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Implement the central Python/FastAPI platform as a modular monolith with explicit domain/module ownership and service interfaces.

Modules share one deployable process and PostgreSQL database initially but SHALL maintain clear internal boundaries so later extraction remains possible.

docs.title: Microservices from day one
docs.text: Rejected due to premature operational complexity, cross-service consistency risk and slower delivery.

docs.title: Unstructured monolith
docs.text: Rejected because domain boundaries would erode and future extraction/testing would be harder.

docs.title: Positive
docs.text:
• simpler deployment/observability/transactions
  • faster cross-domain iteration
  • easier customer-hosted packaging
  • strong transactional consistency for entitlement/allocation/grant workflows

docs.title: Negative / risk
docs.text:
• discipline is required to prevent module coupling
  • scaling is process/database oriented initially
  • module boundaries are architectural rather than infrastructure-enforced

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• controllers do not directly orchestrate unrelated modules
  • cross-module actions use application/use-case services
  • module ownership of tables/services/endpoints is documented
  • internal events/outbox are used for asynchronous external side effects
  • future extraction must preserve contracts rather than copy hidden dependencies

docs.title: Related requirements
docs.text: SDR-PLT-003, SDR-BE-003, SDR-BE-004

docs.title: ADR-003 — Marketplace and OTA Remain Inside LMS
docs.text: Status: Approved Decision class: Product / Platform Architecture

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Feature discovery, trial/purchase eligibility, compatibility, capacity preview, release selection and deployment all depend on the same customer, device, entitlement, policy, capacity and audit data.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Marketplace and OTA SHALL be distinct logical modules within LMS rather than separate standalone products in the initial architecture.

Artifact storage may use an external repository, and delivery infrastructure may later be extracted, but business eligibility and orchestration remain governed by LMS.

docs.title: Separate Marketplace service/application
docs.text: Rejected initially because it would duplicate customer/device/entitlement state and create synchronization complexity.

docs.title: Separate OTA control plane
docs.text: Rejected initially because release eligibility, update rights and device lifecycle already live in LMS.

docs.title: Positive
docs.text:
• one source of truth for eligibility and device state
  • easier trial/purchase-to-deployment flow
  • common audit and authorization model
  • reduced duplicated integration logic

docs.title: Negative / risk
docs.text:
• LMS has broader scope
  • strong internal module boundaries are required
  • scaling of artifact transfer must remain separated from transactional API concerns

docs.title: Related requirements
docs.text: SDR-MKT-001 through SDR-MKT-005, SDR-OTA-*

docs.title: ADR-004 — Traditional Signed Edge Release Packages
docs.text: Status: Approved Decision class: Edge / Release Architecture

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Target deployments include Linux edge devices today and future Windows-compatible environments. Some customer sites are offline/air-gapped. Requiring Docker/container runtime on every edge host would constrain supported environments and add operational dependencies.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Edge application delivery SHALL use manifest-driven traditional signed release packages rather than making Docker a platform dependency.

Packages include signed metadata plus application/UI/dependency/config/migration/install/rollback/health artifacts. Linux handlers are implemented first; interfaces remain compatible with future Windows-native handlers.

Models remain independently versioned/encrypted artifacts and may be coordinated through a Release Set.

docs.title: Docker-only edge deployment
docs.text: Rejected because it would narrow target environments and complicate some customer-hosted/Windows/offline use cases.

docs.title: Manual file-copy installers
docs.text: Rejected because they do not provide deterministic verification, migration, health and rollback semantics.

docs.title: Positive
docs.text:
• works in constrained/offline environments
  • no container runtime dependency
  • package can carry deterministic migration/health/rollback logic
  • future Windows packaging remains feasible

docs.title: Negative / risk
docs.text:
• installer/update manager must handle OS differences explicitly
  • package format/security is more responsibility for LMS/edge team
  • script execution must be tightly constrained

docs.title: Related requirements
docs.text: SDR-PLT-004, SDR-PLT-005, SDR-OTA-006 through SDR-OTA-010

docs.title: Follow-up
docs.text: ADR-010 freezes the exact archive/handler format before Update Manager implementation freeze.

docs.title: ADR-005 — Device-Generated Cryptographic Identity
docs.text: Status: Approved Decision class: Security / Device Lifecycle

docs.title: Context
docs.text: MAC address, hostname or a customer-shared activation code can be copied/spoofed and are insufficient for device-bound grants. Hardware can also change legitimately over device lifetime.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Each device SHALL generate/hold an asymmetric key pair and register its public key with LMS. A versioned weighted hardware fingerprint is supporting identity evidence; MAC/network identifiers are evidence only.

Minor hardware changes are tolerated according to fingerprint policy. Major identity change, key loss or motherboard-level change enters REHOST_REQUIRED and requires controlled approval.

docs.title: MAC-address identity
docs.text: Rejected because MACs are mutable/spoofable and unreliable across replacements.

docs.title: Server-generated shared device secret
docs.text: Rejected because centralized secret distribution increases cloning/custody risk.

docs.title: Exact immutable hardware hash
docs.text: Rejected because legitimate RAM/storage/NIC changes would unnecessarily invalidate devices.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• grants/offline requests can bind to a cryptographic principal
  • cloning becomes harder than copying a license file
  • key storage quality on the edge matters
  • rehost/transfer workflows become explicit business/security processes
  • hardware fingerprint algorithm must be versioned and testable

docs.title: Related requirements
docs.text: SDR-DEV-005 through SDR-DEV-010

docs.title: ADR-006 — Separate License and Release Signing Keys
docs.text: Status: Approved Decision class: Security / Cryptographic Architecture

docs.title: Context
docs.text: License grants and software/model releases represent different trust purposes. Reusing one signing key would increase blast radius and make rotation/incident handling ambiguous.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Use separate cryptographic key purposes and key identities for license/grant signing and software/model release signing. Additional separation for model/key-wrapping operations MAY be introduced without changing this ADR.

docs.title: One platform-wide signing key
docs.text: Rejected because compromise, rotation and authorization policy would affect unrelated trust domains.

docs.title: Application-stored private keys
docs.text: Rejected because normal application/database compromise would become signing compromise.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• reduced compromise blast radius
  • independent rotation/recovery windows
  • distinct authorization policy for signing requests
  • devices must trust/version multiple public-key purposes
  • audit records must include key purpose and key ID

docs.title: Security / operational impact
docs.text: Production private keys remain in KMS/HSM/equivalent protected provider. Trust-store distribution must support overlap between active and retiring verification keys.

docs.title: Related requirements
docs.text: SDR-SEC-003, SDR-SEC-004, SDR-MOD-002

docs.title: ADR-007 — Signed Offline Request/Response Protocol
docs.text: Status: Approved Decision class: Offline / Security Architecture

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Air-gapped devices cannot rely on live API calls. Offline media/relay workstations cannot be trusted with authority to create licenses or release packages.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Offline/air-gapped workflows SHALL use device-signed requests and centrally issued signed response packages bound to request ID, nonce and device identity.

Relay/media components SHALL remain transport-only and SHALL NOT contain signing private keys or authority to alter entitlement/grant state.

docs.title: Protocol properties
docs.text:
• request includes request ID, nonce, device identity reference, current grant/release/model inventory and requested operation
  • central verifies device signature, ownership, request freshness and replay state
  • response is bound to request ID/nonce/device
  • edge verifies signature/hash/binding/revision before use
  • accepted activation/install emits signed receipt for later reconciliation

docs.title: USB license file with no request binding
docs.text: Rejected because replay/cross-device reuse is harder to prevent.

docs.title: Signing on relay workstation
docs.text: Rejected because it turns a portable endpoint into a high-value authority and breaks central commercial governance.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• offline behavior preserves the same trust semantics as online issuance
  • replay/cross-device misuse is bounded
  • fully air-gapped revocation remains delayed until signed import or authorization expiry
  • field operators need deterministic package/error handling

docs.title: Related requirements
docs.text: SDR-OFF-001 through SDR-OFF-009

docs.title: ADR-008 — Production Human Authentication
docs.text: Status: Open Decision Decision class: Security / Identity Architecture

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Local development can begin with username/password authentication, but enterprise production deployments commonly require federation, MFA, account lifecycle and customer identity-provider integration. Authorization/RBAC must not be coupled to one identity provider.

docs.title: Constraints already approved
docs.text:
• authorization evaluates permission + scope independently from authentication provider
  • unique human identities; no shared administrators
  • privileged authentication events are audited
  • privileged/vendor access targets MFA where supported
  • break-glass access is separately controlled and reviewed
  • device identity remains separate from human identity

docs.title: Options to decide
docs.text:
1. OIDC-only production profile
  2. OIDC + SAML adapter boundary if customer demand requires it
  3. vendor-managed local accounts for selected customer-hosted deployments as an exception
  4. MFA enforcement at IdP versus LMS step-up for selected privileged actions

docs.title: Decision criteria
docs.text:
• SaaS and customer-hosted support
  • enterprise IdP compatibility
  • MFA assurance
  • account deprovisioning/revocation
  • offline customer-hosted administration requirements
  • operational complexity
  • supportability

docs.title: Consequence until resolved
docs.text: Implementation SHALL keep authentication behind an adapter and SHALL NOT embed authorization/business rules into username/password-specific code.

docs.title: Decision deadline
docs.text: Must be resolved before production security freeze and external customer onboarding.

docs.title: Related requirements
docs.text: SDR-SEC-001, SDR-SEC-002

docs.title: ADR-009 — Model Encryption and Key Wrapping
docs.text: Status: Open Security Decision Decision class: Security / Model Protection

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Model artifacts are valuable IP and must be distributable through online/offline routes without embedding a universal password. Authorization must tie model use to a valid entitlement/device or deployment context.

docs.title: Baseline already approved
docs.text:
• model artifacts are encrypted and signed
  • random content-encryption keys are preferred per artifact/release
  • entitlement controls permission to use a model
  • device/deployment identity controls authorized unwrap/use
  • plaintext content keys are not stored in normal LMS DB/logs
  • a universal customer-wide/static model password is prohibited

docs.title: Per-device wrapped DEK
docs.text: Strong device binding and revocation granularity; larger metadata/packaging overhead.

docs.title: Per-deployment/site wrapped DEK
docs.text: Lower wrapping overhead; broader compromise scope.

docs.title: Online KMS-assisted unwrap only
docs.text: Strong central control but incompatible with fully air-gapped operation unless offline escrow/derived mechanism exists.

docs.title: Local platform secure storage
docs.text: TPM/secure element/OS key store where available, with fallback profile needed for heterogeneous devices.

docs.title: Required decision output
docs.text: The final ADR amendment/superseding ADR must freeze envelope-encryption algorithm/profile, KEK hierarchy, KMS/HSM integration, wrapping scope, local protected storage, rotation/recovery and offline package behavior.

docs.title: Security considerations
docs.text: Root/administrator compromise may expose plaintext model memory during legitimate execution; encryption protects storage/distribution and raises misuse cost but does not create impossible software-only DRM guarantees.

docs.title: Decision deadline
docs.text: Before production Model OTA implementation/security freeze.

docs.title: Related requirements
docs.text: SDR-MOD-002, SDR-MOD-004, SDR-MOD-005

docs.title: ADR-010 — Release Package Format
docs.text: Status: Proposed Decision class: Edge / Release Format

docs.title: Context
docs.text: ADR-004 selected traditional signed packages instead of a Docker dependency, but the exact archive/container, script-handler contract and platform abstraction must be frozen before Update Manager implementation stabilizes.

docs.title: Proposed baseline
docs.text: A release package contains a signed canonical manifest plus immutable referenced artifacts for application, UI/runtime, dependencies, migrations, configuration templates, install handler, rollback handler and health check. Models may be separate encrypted artifacts referenced by the Release Set.

docs.title: Requirements for the final format
docs.text:
• deterministic/canonical manifest serialization
  • explicit format/schema version
  • bounded archive size/file count/path rules
  • content hashes for every artifact
  • signed handler artifacts; no unsigned inline commands
  • Linux handler implementation first
  • Windows-compatible handler abstraction
  • staged extraction and execution
  • source-version/config-schema compatibility declaration
  • health and rollback contract
  • offline media friendly
  • delta/missing-artifact reuse support

docs.title: Options to decide
docs.text:
1. ZIP-based package
  2. tar-based package with constrained compression
  3. directory/manifests downloaded as separate immutable objects and assembled locally
  4. hybrid bundle with manifest plus externally referenced artifacts

docs.title: Decision criteria
docs.text: Security of extraction, cross-platform implementation, large model handling, offline transport, streaming/delta support, tooling availability and reproducibility.

docs.title: Rejected direction
docs.text: Arbitrary installer scripts copied manually to customer sites are not acceptable.

docs.title: Decision deadline
docs.text: Before Update Manager package parser/executor implementation freeze.

docs.title: Related requirements
docs.text: SDR-PLT-004, SDR-OTA-006 through SDR-OTA-010

docs.title: ADR-011 — Separate Commercial Expiry, Offline Freshness and Grace
docs.text: Status: Approved Decision class: Licensing / Lifecycle

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Subscription expiry, permitted disconnected operation and post-expiry recovery/grace answer different business/technical questions. Combining them into one timestamp would allow check-ins to accidentally extend paid rights or make offline behavior ambiguous.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
LMS SHALL model three independent clocks: commercial term/expiry, offline authorization freshness and grace/restriction period.

A successful check-in may refresh offline authorization only; it SHALL NOT extend commercial expiry. Renewal requires a new commercial term and signed grant revision.

docs.title: One rolling expiry timestamp
docs.text: Rejected because check-in could inadvertently renew commercial rights.

docs.title: No offline freshness limit
docs.text: Rejected because indefinitely disconnected grants weaken revocation/control.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• predictable offline behavior
  • clear renewal semantics
  • separate policy configuration
  • UI/support must display all clocks independently
  • tests must cover combinations of active/expired/stale/grace

docs.title: Related requirements
docs.text: SDR-LIF-001 through SDR-LIF-009

docs.title: ADR-012 — Central Capacity Advisory, Local Capacity Authoritative
docs.text: Status: Approved Decision class: Capacity / Edge Architecture

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Central LMS can plan using reported inventory and benchmark profiles but cannot always see instantaneous streams, resource pressure, driver state or thermal conditions. Commercial entitlement must also remain distinct from hardware feasibility.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Central Capacity Engine SHALL provide advisory pre-assessment. Local Capacity Engine SHALL make the authoritative activation decision using current local workload/runtime evidence.

Capacity failure SHALL NOT silently modify purchased entitlement. The engine returns recommendations and the operator/customer selects an allowed active configuration.

docs.title: Central-only authority
docs.text: Rejected because evidence can be stale and disconnected devices require local decisions.

docs.title: Capacity automatically rewrites license quantity
docs.text: Rejected because technical feasibility and commercial rights are separate domains.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• safer runtime activation
  • consistent offline behavior
  • central UI can plan but must show freshness/confidence
  • local and central assessment contracts must be compatible
  • support must distinguish entitlement from selected active configuration

docs.title: Related requirements
docs.text: SDR-CAP-001 through SDR-CAP-011

docs.title: ADR-013 — Transactional Outbox for External Side Effects
docs.text: Status: Approved Decision class: Backend Reliability

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Grant signing, notifications, ERP synchronization and deployment dispatch depend on external systems that cannot join a PostgreSQL transaction. Performing them inline can leave commercial state inconsistent if the network call succeeds/fails at the wrong time.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Persist business state and an outbox event in the same database transaction. Durable workers deliver external side effects with at-least-once semantics; consumers/actions must be idempotent.

docs.title: Direct external call inside request transaction
docs.text: Rejected because external systems cannot participate atomically and long calls hold DB/request resources.

docs.title: Fire-and-forget in memory
docs.text: Rejected because process restart loses work.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• durable recovery from dependency outages
  • explicit retry/dead-letter handling
  • duplicate delivery must be tolerated
  • operational monitoring of queue age/dead letters is mandatory

docs.title: Related requirements
docs.text: SDR-BE-003, SDR-BE-004, SDR-BE-005

docs.title: ADR-014 — External Artifact Repository, PostgreSQL Metadata Only
docs.text: Status: Approved Decision class: Storage / Release Architecture

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Application/model binaries can be large and should not inflate transactional PostgreSQL storage/backups. SaaS and customer-hosted deployments need different storage providers while retaining common release metadata.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
PostgreSQL stores artifact metadata, references, hashes, signatures, compatibility and lifecycle state. Large binaries SHALL live in an artifact repository abstraction.

SaaS uses S3-compatible/object storage; customer-hosted uses MinIO or another approved repository/provider.

docs.title: Store large binaries as PostgreSQL BLOBs
docs.text: Rejected due to backup/restore growth and poor separation of transactional vs binary storage concerns.

docs.title: Hard-code one cloud object store
docs.text: Rejected because customer-hosted/offline environments require provider flexibility.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• lighter transactional DB
  • provider abstraction required
  • artifact availability/backup monitored separately
  • repository possession is not trust; devices still verify signature/hash

docs.title: Related requirements
docs.text: SDR-OTA-011, SDR-OPS-001

docs.title: ADR-015 — Coherent Release Set as Deployment/Rollback Unit
docs.text: Status: Approved Decision class: Edge / OTA

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Application, plugins/features, UI/runtime, models and configuration schemas can have compatibility dependencies. Rolling back only one component after a failed deployment may leave the product inconsistent.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Deployment and rollback SHALL operate on a coherent Release Set representing compatible application, feature/plugin, UI/runtime, model and configuration versions.

At least the immediately previous known-good Release Set SHALL be preserved; 2–3 known-good sets are preferred when storage permits.

docs.title: Independent component rollback without coordination
docs.text: Rejected because dependency mismatches can make rollback unsafe.

docs.title: No local rollback retention
docs.text: Rejected because air-gapped/failed central connectivity needs autonomous recovery.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• deterministic health/rollback behavior
  • storage reservation required
  • manifests need cross-component compatibility metadata
  • model-only updates still participate in release-set compatibility state

docs.title: Related requirements
docs.text: SDR-OTA-008, SDR-OTA-009, SDR-MOD-007

docs.title: ADR-016 — Tenant Isolation Enforced in Application Authorization
docs.text: Status: Approved Decision class: Security / SaaS Architecture

docs.title: Context
docs.text: SaaS LMS is multi-tenant. Customer/site/device identifiers are externally supplied in APIs and cannot be trusted as proof of access. Customer-hosted mode may be single-customer, but maintaining separate code paths would increase security drift.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Tenant/customer scope SHALL be enforced in authorization and repository/service access paths for all business data, including background jobs, audit queries, offline package generation and deployment targeting.

Customer-hosted mode SHALL keep the same tenant-aware code paths even when only one customer is configured.

docs.title: UI-only filtering
docs.text: Rejected because direct API/object-ID access could bypass it.

docs.title: Separate tenant-specific databases as the only isolation control
docs.text: Rejected as the sole control because application authorization is still required and SaaS/customer-hosted topology may vary.

docs.title: Remove tenant checks in customer-hosted mode
docs.text: Rejected because divergent code paths would create regression/security risk.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• repository/service interfaces require scope context
  • negative tenant-isolation tests are release blockers
  • global/support access must be explicit rather than accidental
  • background workers must carry tenant identity

docs.title: Related requirements
docs.text: SDR-BE-009, SDR-SEC-001, SDR-SEC-007

docs.title: ADR-017 — Separate High-Volume Telemetry from Licensing OLTP
docs.text: Status: Approved Decision class: Data / Operations Architecture

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Licensing, entitlement, grant and audit records require transactional integrity. Usage/performance telemetry can be high-volume, delayed and best-effort. Mixing both concerns in the same operational path would increase database pressure and make licensing dependent on analytics delivery.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Transactional licensing/audit state SHALL remain in the operational PostgreSQL data model. High-volume telemetry SHALL be logically separated and MAY move to a dedicated time-series/analytics/warehouse store as volume requires.

Licensing SHALL NOT depend on successful delivery of best-effort high-volume telemetry.

docs.title: Put all telemetry in core OLTP indefinitely
docs.text: Rejected due to scaling/retention/query interference risk.

docs.title: Make telemetry receipt mandatory for license validity
docs.text: Rejected because offline/air-gapped operation is a first-class requirement.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• clear operational source of truth
  • telemetry pipelines can evolve independently
  • duplicated/aggregated operational events may exist in analytics
  • privacy/residency policy remains separately governable

docs.title: ADR-018 — Same Core LMS Codebase for SaaS and Customer-Hosted
docs.text: Status: Approved Decision class: Product / Deployment Architecture

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The platform must support vendor-operated SaaS and customer-hosted/on-prem deployments. Forking the product would multiply security, release, migration and support cost.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: SaaS and customer-hosted deployments SHALL use the same core LMS application/domain codebase. Differences SHALL be supplied through configuration and provider adapters for identity, artifact storage, signing, email, telemetry and infrastructure topology.

docs.title: Separate SaaS and on-prem forks
docs.text: Rejected because feature/security fixes would diverge and double release/QA effort.

docs.title: SaaS-only control plane with mandatory cloud dependency
docs.text: Rejected because customer-hosted/air-gapped requirements prohibit mandatory vendor connectivity.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• shared domain behavior and test suites
  • deployment providers must have clear interfaces
  • customer-hosted packaging must avoid assumptions about cloud services
  • HA topology may differ without changing business/domain semantics

docs.title: Related requirements
docs.text: SDR-PLT-002, SDR-PLT-006, SDR-PLT-007

docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.text:
The LMS is a modular enterprise control plane. Business truth is centralized; final authorization and installation enforcement remain local.

flowchart TB
    P[Admin / Customer Portal] --> API[Central LMS API]
    API --> REG[Registry & Enrollment]
    API --> ENT[Entitlement Engine]
    API --> POL[Policy Engine]
    API --> CAP[Capacity Service]
    API --> MKT[Marketplace]
    API --> REL[Release / OTA]
    API --> LIFE[Lifecycle / Renewal]
    API --> AUD[Audit & Reporting]
    ENT --> SIGN[Protected Signing Service]
    POL --> SIGN
    REL --> AR[(Artifact Repository)]
    API --> DB[(PostgreSQL)]
    API -->|Online| EDGE[Edge / Server]
    API -->|Signed request-response| RELAY[Authorized Relay]
    RELAY --> EDGE
    EDGE --> ID[Device Identity]
    EDGE --> LA[License Agent]
    EDGE --> LC[Local Capacity Engine]
    EDGE --> UM[Update Manager]
    EDGE --> RT[Analytics Runtime]

docs.title: Responsibility split
docs.text:
• Entitlement Engine: what the customer owns.
  • Policy Engine: under what conditions it may be used.
  • Capacity Engine: what the hardware can run safely.
  • Release/OTA: which software/model artifacts are installed.
  • License Agent: whether the feature may execute.

docs.title: Artifact Storage Architecture
docs.text: PostgreSQL stores transactional metadata and lifecycle state. Large application, UI, dependency and encrypted model binaries live in an external artifact repository through a provider abstraction.

docs.title: Storage abstraction
docs.text:
Release / Model Service
        ↓
Artifact Repository Interface
        ├── SaaS: S3-compatible object storage
        └── Customer-hosted: MinIO / approved filesystem-object provider

docs.title: PostgreSQL
docs.text: Stores artifact ID, release/model association, logical type, immutable version, repository reference, size, content hash, signature/key ID, encryption profile, compatibility, publish/retire state and audit linkage.

docs.title: Artifact repository
docs.text: Stores immutable binary bytes and supports controlled put/get/head, retention/versioning/backup according to provider capability.

docs.title: Signing provider
docs.text: Signs manifests/artifacts or hashes according to release format. Artifact storage itself never possesses signing authority.

docs.title: Publication flow
docs.text:
1. upload/stage candidate bytes
  2. validate size/type/security constraints
  3. compute content hash
  4. create release/model metadata
  5. build canonical manifest
  6. obtain protected signature
  7. mark artifact/release Published atomically at metadata level
  8. published bytes become immutable

docs.title: Immutability
docs.text: A Published artifact is never replaced in place. Correction creates a new artifact/release identity/version. Repository object versioning may retain old bytes but LMS lifecycle state governs new deployment eligibility.

docs.title: Integrity and download
docs.text: Edge trusts the signed manifest and expected content hash, not repository location. Downloaded/imported bytes are verified before install/decryption. Existing local content is reused only when identity/version/hash match.

docs.title: Access control
docs.text: Central service uses least-privilege repository credentials. Pre-signed/temporary URLs, if used, are short-lived and scoped. Direct bucket/container listing is not a customer authorization mechanism.

docs.title: Encryption
docs.text: Provider-side encryption at rest is used where supported. Model artifacts additionally use application-level model encryption according to the model protection design.

docs.title: Retention and deletion
docs.text: Retired releases may be retained for rollback/support/DR according to policy. Deletion must not remove content still referenced by supported releases, active deployments or required rollback sets.

docs.title: Backup/DR
docs.text: Repository backup/versioning/replication is tested together with PostgreSQL metadata recovery. Restore validation verifies hashes and referential availability.

docs.title: Related SDR/ADR
docs.text: SDR-OTA-006, SDR-OTA-011, SDR-OPS-001; ADR-014

docs.title: Configuration & Policy Hierarchy
docs.text: The platform resolves policy deterministically across platform, product, customer/entitlement, site and device scopes. Lower-level overrides are allowed only for explicitly overrideable keys and can never weaken non-relaxable security controls.

docs.title: Resolution order
docs.text:
Platform Default
    ↓
Product Override
    ↓
Customer / Entitlement Override
    ↓
Site Override
    ↓
Device Override

For a key not specified at a lower scope, the nearest higher-scope value is inherited.

docs.title: Policy metadata
docs.text: Every policy key should define: - key/name - data type/unit - default value - allowed scope(s) - min/max/enum constraints - whether lower scopes may override - whether stricter-only override is required - whether maker-checker is required - effective-from/expiry where relevant

docs.title: Policy domains
docs.text:
• offline authorization duration
  • grace duration
  • trial duration and eligibility
  • release channel eligibility
  • AUTO/MANUAL OTA
  • maintenance window
  • rollout concurrency/batch size
  • rollback behavior
  • model-only update permission
  • notification preferences
  • audit retention
  • capacity warning/override policy
  • telemetry delivery/retention policy when approved

docs.title: Example resolved policy
docs.text:
{
  "offline_days": 7,
  "grace_days": 7,
  "trial_days": 7,
  "ota_mode": "auto",
  "release_channel": "stable",
  "maintenance_window": {"start": "01:00", "end": "03:00", "timezone": "site"},
  "auto_rollback": true,
  "model_only_updates": true
}

The 7-day trial shown above is the platform default. A customer/product campaign may resolve another value only through an allowed, auditable override.

docs.title: Resolved-policy response
docs.text: Operators need to know not only the effective value but where it came from. Resolved policy should expose source scope, source object ID/revision and whether the value is inherited/overridden.

docs.title: Conflict rules
docs.text:
• invalid lower-scope values are rejected, not silently clamped
  • expired overrides fall back to inherited policy
  • non-relaxable security minima cannot be overridden
  • an approval-bound override is invalid if the target revision/payload changes
  • device-specific exception must not mutate customer-wide policy

docs.title: Change/audit
docs.text: Sensitive policy changes generate audit events with previous/effective value, source scope, actor/reason and approval reference. Policy revision is included in downstream grant/deployment evidence where behavior depends on it.

docs.title: Related SDR
docs.text: SDR-TRL-001, SDR-LIF-002, SDR-LIF-003, SDR-OTA-004, SDR-OTA-005, SDR-SEC-008

docs.title: Deployment Models
docs.text: The same LMS application architecture supports SaaS and customer-hosted deployments with configuration/provider adapters rather than separate product forks.

docs.title: SaaS baseline
docs.text:
• multi-tenant logical isolation
  • Phase 1 single-primary application/database baseline
  • automated encrypted backups and tested restore
  • externalized artifact repository
  • protected signing provider
  • health monitoring and alerting
  • design remains horizontally/HA evolvable without changing domain model

docs.title: Customer-hosted baseline
docs.text:
• same application codebase
  • isolated customer deployment
  • customer-managed or vendor-approved PostgreSQL/artifact storage/signing integration
  • manual signed LMS upgrade package initially
  • outbound dependencies minimized and explicitly documented
  • HA optional enterprise deployment profile
  • customer environment may be disconnected from vendor SaaS

docs.title: Edge connectivity modes
docs.text:
1. Online — device communicates directly with LMS.
  2. Assisted offline — authorized relay transports signed request/response data.
  3. Fully air-gapped — controlled media carries signed request/response packages.

All routes use the same grant/artifact trust model; connectivity mode changes transport, not authorization semantics.

docs.title: Deployment dependencies
docs.text: Dependency SaaS Customer-hosted Failure effect PostgreSQL vendor managed customer/vendor managed LMS writes unavailable; no unsigned fallback Artifact storage object storage MinIO/approved repository package delivery unavailable Signing provider KMS/HSM/equivalent approved protected provider new grant/release signing blocked Email provider SMTP/relay notifications delayed only ERP optional integration optional integration reconciliation/commercial import delayed Telemetry store separate/optional separate/optional analytics delayed; licensing unaffected

docs.title: Network exposure principle
docs.text: Only required interfaces are exposed. Edge local APIs remain local by default. Customer-hosted network/port matrix must be generated by deployment packaging before production release.

docs.title: Upgrade principle
docs.text: Central LMS upgrade and edge product OTA are separate lifecycles. Customer-hosted LMS upgrades are manual package operations initially; edge application/model updates remain managed through LMS release/deployment functions.

docs.title: Core Sequence Diagrams
docs.text: This page defines implementation-level interaction expectations between the central LMS and edge/application components.

docs.title: First-time registration and base activation
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    actor A as Vendor Admin
    participant P as LMS Portal/API
    participant D as Device Agent
    participant R as Device Registry
    participant C as Capacity Service
    participant E as Entitlement Engine
    participant S as Signing Service
    participant L as Local License Agent
    A->>P: Create customer/site + enrollment authorization
    D->>P: Enrollment request + public key + fingerprint + inventory
    P->>R: Validate token, ownership, duplicates
    R-->>P: Registered device identity
    P->>C: Pre-assess base workload
    C-->>P: Advisory result
    P->>E: Check approved commercial entitlement
    E-->>P: Entitlement + limits
    P->>S: Sign device-bound base grant
    S-->>P: Signed grant
    P-->>D: Deliver grant
    D->>L: Import grant
    L->>L: Verify signature, binding, term, revision

docs.title: Online trial activation
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    actor U as Customer Admin
    participant M as Marketplace
    participant P as Policy/Entitlement
    participant C as Capacity
    participant R as Release Service
    participant D as Device
    U->>M: Start trial
    M->>P: Validate eligibility (customer entitlement + feature)
    P-->>M: Eligible + configured duration
    M->>C: Pre-assess workload
    C-->>M: Recommendation/result
    M->>R: Resolve compatible release/model set
    M-->>D: Signed trial grant + required artifacts
    D->>D: Verify + local capacity + install + health-check

docs.title: Offline / air-gapped trial activation
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant D as Device
    participant O as Relay/Media
    participant L as LMS
    participant S as Signing/Artifacts
    D->>O: Export signed trial request + nonce + inventory
    O->>L: Transfer request
    L->>L: Validate trial eligibility + capacity pre-assessment
    L->>S: Create signed trial grant + minimal compatible bundle
    S-->>L: Response package
    L-->>O: Approved response
    O-->>D: Controlled-media import

docs.text:
sequenceDiagram

    participant M as Marketplace
    participant E as ERP/Commercial
    participant L as LMS Entitlement/Policy
    participant R as Release Service
    participant D as Device
    U->>M: Request purchase
    M->>E: Commercial approval/payment workflow
    E-->>L: Approved commercial state
    L->>L: Create/update entitlement item + allocation
    L->>L: Issue superseding/add-on grant
    L->>R: Resolve compatible package/model set

    L-->>D: Grant + release set

docs.title: Capacity reassessment after hardware/workload change
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant D as Device
    participant C as Central Capacity
    participant L as Local Capacity
    participant A as Admin
    D->>C: New inventory/resource/workload snapshot
    C->>C: Recalculate using benchmark profile
    C-->>A: Pass/warning/fail + recommendations
    A->>D: Choose approved configuration if adjustment needed
    D->>L: Reassess actual local combined workload
    L-->>D: Authoritative activation decision
    Note over D,L: Commercial entitlement is unchanged

docs.title: Online software/model update
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant L as LMS Deployment
    participant D as Update Manager
    participant R as Runtime
    L-->>D: Deployment target + signed release-set manifest
    D->>D: Preflight license/compatibility/disk/capacity
    D->>L: Fetch only missing artifacts/models
    D->>D: Verify signatures/hashes
    D->>D: Preserve known-good release set
    D->>D: Stage + migrate
    D->>R: Restart/start target services
    R-->>D: Health result
    alt Health OK
      D->>D: Commit target release set
      D-->>L: Installation receipt
    else Health failed
      D->>D: Roll back coherent previous release set
      D-->>L: Failure/rollback receipt
    end

docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant D as Device
    participant O as Relay/Media
    participant L as LMS
    D->>O: Export request + installed release/model inventory
    O->>L: Import request
    L->>L: Resolve minimal delta bundle
    L-->>O: Signed release set + only missing artifacts
    O-->>D: Import package
    D->>D: Verify + preflight + stage + migrate + health-check

      D->>D: Commit
    else Failure
      D->>D: Rollback
    end
    D-->>O: Signed installation receipt
    O-->>L: Reconcile

sequenceDiagram

    participant L as LMS
    participant S as Signing Service
    participant O as Offline Relay
    participant D as Device

    L-->>O: Export response package
    O-->>D: Controlled-media transfer

    D-->>O: Signed acceptance receipt
    O-->>L: Reconcile receipt

docs.text:
sequenceDiagram

    participant O as Old Device
    participant N as New/Changed Device
    participant L as LMS
    A->>L: Submit replacement/rehost request
    N->>L: Register new cryptographic identity/fingerprint
    L->>L: Validate ownership + approval + allocation
    L->>L: Retire/suspend old binding
    L->>L: Reassign/return allocation
    L-->>N: New device-bound superseding grant

    N-->>L: Acceptance receipt

docs.title: Device transfer
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    actor A as Requester
    actor B as Approver
    participant L as LMS
    participant D as Device
    A->>L: Request customer/site transfer
    L->>L: Validate current rights and target ownership
    L-->>B: Maker-checker approval request
    B->>L: Approve
    L->>L: Supersede invalid old grants + update ownership/site assignments
    L-->>D: New valid grant/policy state

docs.text:
sequenceDiagram

    participant L as LMS
    participant D as Connected Device
    participant O as Air-gapped Device
    A->>L: Revoke grant/device
    L->>L: Record revocation + superseding state
    L-->>D: Deliver at sync/check-in
    D->>D: Enforce revoke

docs.title: Failed update and rollback
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant L as LMS
    participant D as Update Manager
    participant R as Runtime
    L-->>D: Target release set
    D->>D: Verify + stage + install
    D->>R: Health check
    R-->>D: FAIL
    D->>D: Restore previous app/plugin/UI/model/config set
    D->>R: Verify rollback health
    alt Rollback healthy
      D-->>L: Rolled-back receipt
    else Rollback failed
      D-->>L: Critical failure receipt / escalate
    end

docs.title: Check-in freshness expiry
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant D as Device
    participant L as License Agent
    D->>L: Runtime authorization check
    L->>L: Compare last successful authorized check-in to policy
    alt Fresh
      L-->>D: Continue
    else Stale but grace/revalidation policy allows restricted state
      L-->>D: Restricted/grace + recovery path
    else Authorization no longer valid
      L-->>D: Disable unauthorized analytics; preserve recovery/diagnostics where allowed
    end

docs.title: Commercial expiry and grace
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant R as Runtime
    participant L as License Agent
    R->>L: Feature authorization request
    L->>L: Evaluate commercial valid_until independently from offline freshness
    alt Commercial term active
      L-->>R: Allow subject to other gates
    else Expired and grace active
      L-->>R: Grace/restricted behavior per policy
    else Expired and grace ended
      L-->>R: Deny analytics execution; keep recovery/diagnostics where allowed
    end

docs.title: State Machines
docs.text: State transitions are explicit, auditable and transactional where business integrity requires it.

docs.title: Device
docs.text:
PENDING -> REGISTERED -> ACTIVE -> SUSPENDED -> RETIRED
                         |
                         +-> REHOST_REQUIRED

docs.title: Grant / License
docs.text:
DRAFT -> ISSUED -> DELIVERED -> ACCEPTED -> ACTIVE -> GRACE -> EXPIRED
                                               |
                                               +-> REVOKED

ISSUED does not mean the device has received it. DELIVERED does not mean the device accepted it.

docs.title: Trial
docs.text:
ELIGIBLE -> REQUESTED -> ISSUED -> ACTIVE -> EXPIRED
                                      |
                                      +-> CONVERTED

Trial time begins when activation succeeds, not when the request or grant is issued.

docs.title: Purchase Request
docs.text:
REQUESTED -> REVIEW -> APPROVED -> PAID/COMMERCIAL_CONFIRMED -> GRANT_ISSUED
                  |
                  +-> REJECTED

A purchase request or catalog entry never authorizes execution by itself.

docs.title: Offline Request / Response
docs.text:
CREATED -> EXPORTED -> RECEIVED -> APPROVED -> RESPONSE_ISSUED -> IMPORTED -> RECONCILED
                           |            |
                           |            +-> REJECTED
                           +-> EXPIRED

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
AVAILABLE -> DOWNLOADED/IMPORTED -> VERIFIED -> STAGED -> INSTALLING -> HEALTH_CHECK -> ACTIVE
                                                              |             |
                                                              |             +-> ROLLED_BACK
                                                              +-> FAILED

docs.title: Renewal
docs.text:
DUE_SOON -> REQUESTED -> APPROVED_GRANT_ISSUED -> DELIVERED_IMPORTED -> ACCEPTED_ACTIVE
                |                   |                     |
                +-> REJECTED       +-> FAILED            +-> FAILED
                                                            |
                                                            +-> EXPIRED_RESTRICTED

docs.title: Governance rule
docs.text: Any implementation-specific state must map cleanly to these business states or be documented as an internal sub-state. UI/API must not collapse distinct business milestones that affect support or audit.

docs.title: System Context & External Boundaries
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    VA[Vendor Admin / Support / Release] --> LMS[LMS Control Plane]
    CA[Customer / Site Admin] --> LMS
    ERP[ERP / Billing] <--> LMS
    IDP[Future OIDC / SSO IdP] --> LMS
    SMTP[Email / Notification Provider] <--> LMS
    STORE[(Artifact Repository)] <--> LMS
    KMS[Protected Signing / KMS-HSM] <--> LMS
    LMS <--> EDGE[Edge Devices / Servers]
    RELAY[Authorized Offline Relay] <--> LMS
    RELAY <--> EDGE
    LMS --> OBS[Monitoring / Logs / Audit Export]

docs.title: Ownership boundaries
docs.text:
• LMS owns operational entitlement, grant, deployment, capacity and lifecycle state.
  • ERP owns financial/order truth when integrated.
  • Signing provider owns protected private-key operations.
  • Artifact repository stores immutable release/model binaries, not commercial truth.
  • Edge owns final local license verification, actual runtime capacity validation and installation commit/rollback.
  • Relay transports signed packages and has no issuance authority.

docs.title: Trust boundaries
docs.text: Human portal sessions, device cryptographic identity, signing infrastructure, artifact storage and offline media are separate trust zones. Data crossing each boundary is authenticated, authorized and validated according to the relevant security section.

docs.title: Failure-domain principle
docs.text: Loss of a non-critical external dependency should not silently corrupt licensing state. Email failure must not undo a renewal; telemetry failure must not invalidate a license; artifact-store failure must not mutate entitlement; signing failure queues/retries issuance rather than producing unsigned grants.

docs.title: System Design Requirements (SDR)
docs.text: This section is the normative, testable design-requirement baseline for LMS. It converts the architecture and business rules into uniquely identified requirements that engineering, QA, security and operations can trace to implementation and acceptance evidence.

docs.title: Requirement language
docs.text:
• SHALL = mandatory requirement.
  • SHOULD = expected unless an approved exception exists.
  • MAY = optional capability.
  • Every SHALL requirement must be traceable to implementation and verification evidence before production release.

docs.title: 1. Platform and deployment requirements
docs.text: ID Requirement Verification SDR-PLT-001 LMS SHALL provide one reusable control plane for current and future enterprise AI products. architecture review + product onboarding test SDR-PLT-002 SaaS and customer-hosted LMS SHALL use the same core domain/application codebase except for deployment/provider adapters. code/config review SDR-PLT-003 The central backend SHALL begin as a modular monolith with explicit bounded modules rather than mandatory microservices. architecture review SDR-PLT-004 Edge application releases SHALL not require Docker as the runtime packaging dependency. package/install test SDR-PLT-005 Linux SHALL be supported first while edge abstractions SHALL preserve a future Windows implementation path. interface/package review SDR-PLT-006 LMS SHALL support online, assisted-offline and fully air-gapped device operations. end-to-end tests SDR-PLT-007 Customer-hosted LMS upgrades SHALL be supported using a signed/manual package process in the initial release. upgrade test

docs.title: 2. Customer, site and device requirements
docs.text: ID Requirement Verification SDR-DEV-001 LMS SHALL model Customer, Site and Device as separate identities with immutable IDs. schema/API test SDR-DEV-002 A device SHALL have one commercial customer owner at a time. DB constraint/service test SDR-DEV-003 A device MAY serve multiple sites through explicit device-site assignments. topology test SDR-DEV-004 Device registration SHALL be independent from commercial licensing and capacity validation. state/API test SDR-DEV-005 Device identity SHALL use a device-generated asymmetric key plus a versioned hardware fingerprint. enrollment test SDR-DEV-006 MAC/network addresses SHALL be supporting evidence only and SHALL NOT be the primary identity. security review/test SDR-DEV-007 Enrollment authorizations SHALL be high-entropy, short-lived and single-use. negative/security test SDR-DEV-008 Minor hardware changes SHALL trigger re-evaluation without mandatory rehost when identity remains within tolerance. hardware-change test SDR-DEV-009 Major identity changes such as motherboard replacement or device-key loss SHALL enter REHOST_REQUIRED. rehost test SDR-DEV-010 Device transfer SHALL be explicit, authorized and auditable; ownership SHALL NOT be silently overwritten. transfer workflow test SDR-DEV-011 Decommission/replacement SHALL return or reconcile eligible allocations before final retirement. lifecycle test

docs.title: 3. Entitlement, allocation and grant requirements
docs.text: ID Requirement Verification SDR-LIC-001 LMS SHALL distinguish Entitlement, Allocation and Grant. domain/schema review SDR-LIC-002 Entitlement SHALL represent customer-owned commercial rights. domain/API test SDR-LIC-003 Allocation SHALL distribute pooled rights to device/site scope without exceeding approved entitlement quantity. transactional concurrency test SDR-LIC-004 Grant SHALL be the signed executable authorization bound to a device. grant verification test SDR-LIC-005 Commercial rights SHALL NOT be encoded as product-specific boolean columns such as ppe_enabled. schema review SDR-LIC-006 Dynamic constraints SHALL support quantity, site, model/runtime and dependency restrictions. policy/grant tests SDR-LIC-007 Replacement grants SHALL use revision and supersession semantics. anti-rollback test SDR-LIC-008 Devices SHALL reject older grant revisions in an accepted grant lineage unless an explicitly signed recovery mechanism permits otherwise. rollback attack test SDR-LIC-009 Subscription and perpetual base entitlements SHALL both be representable without schema redesign. model/API test SDR-LIC-010 Perpetual licenses SHALL support explicit update-right policies. policy test SDR-LIC-011 A device serving multiple sites SHALL be able to receive device-bound grants containing site-specific limits. multi-site grant test

docs.title: 4. Trial and add-on requirements
docs.text: ID Requirement Verification SDR-TRL-001 Default trial duration SHALL be 7 days and SHALL be policy configurable. policy test SDR-TRL-002 Trial time SHALL begin at first successful feature activation, not at request, issuance or package import. lifecycle test SDR-TRL-003 Baseline eligibility SHALL permit one trial per customer entitlement + feature unless an approved policy/campaign override exists. eligibility test SDR-TRL-004 Trials SHALL be implemented as signed time-limited grants. grant test SDR-TRL-005 Globally reusable trial licenses SHALL be prohibited. security review SDR-ADD-001 Subscription add-ons SHALL co-terminate with the active base subscription by default. term-calculation test SDR-ADD-002 Product/commercial policy MAY define explicitly independent add-ons with separate terms. policy test SDR-ADD-003 A perpetual base SHALL support subscription add-ons. lifecycle test SDR-ADD-004 A dependent add-on SHALL become dormant when its required base is inactive unless explicitly independent. dependency test

docs.title: 5. Time, renewal and revocation requirements

docs.title: Trust Boundaries
docs.text: The LMS has multiple trust zones. Security decisions must be based on which boundary data crosses, not only whether a request is 'internal'.

docs.title: Trust zones
docs.text: Zone Trusted for Not trusted for Human browser/session authenticated user intent after authn/authz tenant/object authority without server checks LMS application business policy/orchestration production signing private-key custody PostgreSQL transactional state signing authority or executable artifact trust Artifact repository immutable artifact storage deciding entitlement or execution rights Signing service/KMS/HSM protected cryptographic operations commercial policy decisions Edge device local enforcement/actual runtime evidence central commercial truth Offline relay/media transport only signing, entitlement or device authority ERP commercial/order truth where integrated device grant/runtime truth

docs.title: Central boundary
docs.text: Commercial authorization is evaluated centrally. The application sends an authorized signing request to the protected signing boundary; it never loads raw production signing private keys.

docs.title: Edge boundary
docs.text: The edge verifies signature, key trust, subject binding, commercial term, revision/supersession, dependencies, offline freshness/grace, package/model integrity, compatibility and local capacity before execution.

docs.title: Offline boundary
docs.text:
Offline request/response packages must be safe even if the relay/media is untrusted.

sequenceDiagram
    participant D as Device
    participant R as Relay / Media
    participant L as LMS
    participant S as Signing Service
    D->>D: Generate request_id + nonce + signed request
    D->>R: Export request
    R->>L: Transport only
    L->>L: Validate tenant/device/policy/replay
    L->>S: Authorized signing request
    S-->>L: Signed grant/manifest
    L-->>R: Device-bound response package
    R-->>D: Controlled-media transfer
    D->>D: Verify signature/hash/request binding/revision
    D->>D: Local capacity + install/health
    D-->>R: Signed receipt

docs.title: Boundary rules
docs.text:
• every cross-zone input is authenticated/validated according to its trust source
  • object IDs are not authorization
  • artifact location is not proof of integrity
  • relay possession is not proof of device authorization
  • database possession is not signing authority
  • local device reports are evidence and may be stale/tampered on a compromised host
  • telemetry failure does not alter commercial entitlement
  • email/notification failure does not roll back business transactions

docs.title: Failure containment
docs.text: External dependency failures use transactional outbox/retry rather than corrupting commercial state. Signing outage blocks new signed issuance but does not invalidate already valid grants. Artifact outage blocks delivery, not entitlement. ERP outage delays reconciliation, not local device enforcement.

docs.title: Architectural rules
docs.text:
1. Each endpoint has one owning module.
  2. Controllers validate/authorize and delegate; cross-domain orchestration lives in application/use-case services.
  3. Commercially atomic changes use one DB transaction where possible.
  4. External side effects use outbox/jobs instead of weakening DB consistency.
  5. Tenant scope is explicit in service/repository interfaces.
  6. Public API contracts remain backward-compatible within /v1.
  7. Long-running deployment/bundle work is represented by durable jobs/resources.
  8. Signing private keys are never loaded into backend process memory from normal configuration.

docs.title: Data ownership
docs.text: PostgreSQL owns transactional LMS state. Artifact repository owns immutable large binaries. Telemetry may use separate analytics storage. ERP remains external financial truth. Signing provider owns private cryptographic operations.

docs.title: Reliability model
docs.text: External dependency failures are retried/idempotent. Dead-letter work is visible. Request IDs correlate API, audit, outbox/job and edge receipt flows.

docs.title: Security model
docs.text: Human/device/service principals are distinct. Authorization is permission + tenant/object scope. Background jobs carry scope. All privileged mutations are audited.

docs.title: Grant issuance
docs.text: POST /v1/grants/issue is privileged/internal. It consumes an approved entitlement/allocation/policy snapshot and must be idempotent. Direct client-supplied limits are not trusted without policy validation.

docs.title: Protocol and versioning
docs.text:
• HTTPS outside local development
  • REST/JSON baseline with /v1 major version prefix
  • explicit content type and UTF-8
  • UTC ISO-8601 timestamps
  • opaque IDs; clients do not parse identifier structure
  • breaking semantic changes require new major API version or migration contract

docs.title: Authentication principals
docs.text: Human API calls use the configured human identity/session mechanism. Device APIs use registered device cryptographic identity or an explicitly documented enrollment bootstrap flow. Internal workers use dedicated least-privilege service identities.

docs.title: Authorization
docs.text: Every protected endpoint evaluates permission plus customer/product/site/device/object scope. Client-supplied tenant identifiers never grant access.

docs.title: Common headers
docs.text:
Authorization: Bearer <token>       # human/service where applicable
X-Request-ID: <uuid>
Idempotency-Key: <opaque-uuid>      # retry-safe write workflows

Device-signed endpoints may additionally carry key ID/signature/nonce fields in their canonical request envelope.

docs.title: Request rules
docs.text:
• schema validation at boundary
  • maximum payload/upload sizes
  • unknown critical fields rejected where signed canonicalization requires strictness
  • pagination/filter limits on collections
  • optimistic revision supplied for concurrent mutable resources where needed

docs.title: Response rules
docs.text: Successful responses use a consistent data + meta envelope. Errors use the stable error model. Security-sensitive failures may intentionally generalize external messages.

docs.title: Idempotency
docs.text: Required for grant issuance, activation, offline import, payment/commercial callbacks, deployment creation and other retried write workflows. Same key + different request hash is rejected.

docs.title: Pagination
docs.text: Cursor pagination is preferred for large/ordered collections. APIs define stable sort order, maximum page size and tenant-scoped filters.

docs.title: Long-running operations
docs.text: Release builds, large deployments, offline bundle generation and other long operations return a job/resource identifier rather than holding an HTTP request open. Job state is durable and observable.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: Additive optional fields are allowed within /v1. Removal, type changes, changed meaning, newly required fields or changed security semantics require explicit compatibility handling.

docs.title: Endpoint catalogue
docs.text: The authoritative inventory is maintained in API Endpoint Catalogue; generated OpenAPI becomes the executable contract once implementation begins.

docs.title: Approval & Maker-Checker Workflows
docs.text: Approval workflows separate intent from execution for actions where one mistaken or compromised account could materially affect commercial rights, security posture or fleet operation.

docs.title: Workflow model
docs.text:
DRAFT -> SUBMITTED -> APPROVED -> EXECUTING -> EXECUTED
          |            |             |
          +-> REJECTED +-> EXPIRED   +-> FAILED
          +-> CANCELLED

docs.title: Approval record
docs.text: Every approval captures: - approval/request ID - action type - target object IDs - exact requested payload or immutable payload hash - target object revision - requester - required approver role/separation - reason/business justification - submitted/approved/executed timestamps - expiry - decision comment - execution result/error/audit reference

docs.title: Binding rule
docs.text: Approval applies only to the reviewed payload/object revision. If entitlement quantity, target device, grant term, release, capacity override scope or other material parameters change, the approval becomes invalid and must be resubmitted.

docs.title: Single-actor operations
docs.text: Examples where policy can allow one authorized actor: - allocate quantity within already approved entitlement pool - normal device registration - standard renewal after approved commercial status - publish Development/QA release - routine customer/site metadata edit

docs.title: Maker-checker operations
docs.text: At minimum evaluate/require separation for: - create/increase entitlement outside approved ERP/order automation - perpetual/exceptional custom grant - trial extension/repeat outside policy - cross-customer transfer - major rehost - capacity/security override - Stable promotion and LTS designation - forced broad production rollout - mass revocation - signing-key activation/rotation - trust-bundle/key revocation - model KEK/wrapping administration - break-glass or high-risk audit export

docs.title: Execution
docs.text: Approval does not itself mutate business state. An authorized execution service revalidates: approval status/expiry, object revision, caller/system permission and current business invariants before applying the action transactionally.

docs.title: Automation
docs.text: ERP-approved or policy-approved automation may satisfy selected approval steps only when the automation identity, source event, rules and audit evidence are explicitly approved. 'Automated' does not mean 'uncontrolled'.

docs.title: Failure/retry
docs.text: Execution failure leaves an explicit failed/pending state. Retrying uses idempotent execution and does not create duplicate entitlements/grants/releases.

docs.title: Retention
docs.text: Baseline retention is configurable 1–3 years. Customer/regulatory requirements may extend it. Deletion/retention jobs must themselves be audited.

docs.title: Background Jobs & Scheduler
docs.text: Background execution is a first-class backend subsystem with durable, idempotent jobs.

docs.title: Job families
docs.text:
• renewal reminders
  • trial expiry processing
  • stale offline-check-in detection
  • grace/restriction transitions
  • grant delivery/reconciliation retries
  • notification delivery
  • ERP reconciliation
  • deployment orchestration and rollout scheduling
  • artifact retention/cleanup
  • telemetry aggregation/export
  • audit retention/export
  • capacity reassessment requests triggered by reported changes

docs.title: Reliability rules
docs.text:
• Jobs are idempotent.
  • Durable job state survives application restart.
  • Retryable failures use bounded exponential backoff.
  • Non-retryable validation/security failures enter failed/dead-letter state.
  • A job records customer/tenant scope explicitly.
  • Duplicate execution must not issue duplicate grants or double-apply entitlement changes.
  • Jobs that cause external side effects use the transactional outbox pattern where appropriate.

docs.title: Scheduling
docs.text: Time-based jobs use UTC internally. Customer/site timezone is applied for maintenance windows and user-facing schedules.

docs.title: Observability
docs.text: Expose queue depth, oldest-pending age, success/failure/retry rate and dead-letter count per job family.

docs.title: Operational ownership
docs.text: Support/operations can retry or cancel only approved job classes. Privileged reprocessing that can alter commercial/license state is audited and may require approval.

docs.title: Database Schema — Detailed Baseline

docs.title: Mandatory database controls
docs.text:
• All business tables carry customer/tenant ownership directly or through an enforceable FK path.
  • Allocation updates and grant supersession occur in a single business transaction where possible.
  • Idempotency keys have unique constraints at the workflow boundary.
  • Mutable business objects carry revision/version columns for optimistic concurrency.
  • Audit events are append-only.
  • UTC is used for persisted timestamps; site timezone is display/scheduling context only.

docs.title: Database Design
docs.text: PostgreSQL stores transactional LMS business truth. The schema separates commercial rights, device identity, runtime evidence, release/deployment state and audit rather than collapsing them into one device record.

docs.title: Identity/topology
docs.text: Customer owns sites and devices. Device-site relationships are explicit assignments so one device may serve multiple sites without changing commercial ownership.

docs.title: Commercial licensing
docs.text: Entitlement/entitlement items define purchased rights. Allocations distribute pooled quantity. Grants are signed device-bound runtime artifacts derived from entitlement/allocation/policy.

docs.title: Capacity evidence
docs.text: Stable hardware inventory, dynamic resource snapshots, workload profiles, benchmark profiles and capacity assessments are distinct tables/records so assessments remain reproducible.

docs.title: Release/deployment
docs.text: Feature/model releases and artifact metadata are immutable after publication. Deployment job is central orchestration state; installation receipt is device evidence.

docs.title: Audit/integration
docs.text: Audit events are append-only. ERP/outbox/idempotency records support safe integration/retry without changing commercial truth silently.

docs.title: Integrity requirements
docs.text:
• immutable opaque IDs
  • foreign keys for ownership/lineage
  • UTC timestamps
  • tenant/customer ownership path on business data
  • check/unique constraints for invariants where possible
  • optimistic revision on mutable aggregates
  • explicit grant supersession
  • transactional allocation/reallocation
  • unique idempotency key + request hash
  • append-only audit semantics

docs.title: Transaction boundaries
docs.text:
One business transaction is used for entitlement allocation changes, grant supersession metadata, decommission + allocation return, approval execution and other operations where partial DB success would violate commercial truth.

External signing/storage/email/ERP calls do not run as fake distributed transactions; the outbox/job pattern bridges those boundaries.

docs.title: JSON usage
docs.text: JSON columns are permitted for bounded/extensible evidence and policy attributes such as hardware details or reason lists, but core ownership, quantities, revisions, statuses and relationships remain relational.

docs.title: Migration principles
docs.text: Alembic is the only supported migration path. Risky changes use expand-and-contract. Customer-hosted upgrade manifests declare supported source schema/app versions.

docs.title: Performance/indexing
docs.text: Indexes follow real access patterns such as tenant+status, device+time, grants by device/status/expiry, deployment target status and audit time/object lookups. Final indexes are verified using production-like plans and scale tests.
