docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• Error codes are documented and never repurposed.
  • retryable reflects workflow semantics, not only HTTP class.
  • Security-sensitive reasons may be intentionally generalized externally while full detail is written to audit/secure logs.
  • Offline import errors must be deterministic enough for field operators to recover without site debugging.

docs.title: Database Indexing, Transactions & Concurrency
docs.text: Tier-1 reliability depends on explicit concurrency behaviour, not only schema shape.

docs.title: Transaction boundaries
docs.text:
Use one database transaction for operations where partial success would violate commercial truth, including: - entitlement-pool reallocation across multiple devices - grant revision + supersession record creation - renewal term update + grant issuance record preparation - device decommission + allocation return - approval execution state transitions

External calls such as signing and artifact storage should use an outbox/saga-style pattern when they cannot participate in the DB transaction.

docs.title: Optimistic concurrency
docs.text: Mutable aggregates carry revision or version. Update commands include expected revision. A mismatch returns a conflict rather than overwriting concurrent changes.

docs.title: Initial index strategy
docs.text:
• unique(customer_id, external_reference) where integration keys apply
  • unique(device_id, active key status constraint)
  • index(customer_id, status) on customer-scoped collections
  • index(device_id, collected_at desc) for inventory/snapshots
  • unique(entitlement_id, feature_id, active pool identity) as model permits
  • index(grants: device_id, status, valid_until)
  • unique(grant_id, revision)
  • index(capacity_assessments: device_id, assessed_at desc)
  • unique(feature_id, version) and unique(model_id, version)
  • index(deployment_targets: job_id, status)
  • index(audit_events: customer_id, occurred_at desc) and object lookup indexes

Exact indexes must be validated against production-like query plans before launch.

docs.title: Idempotency storage
docs.text: Persist key, operation, request hash, response reference, created_at and expiry. Same key + different request hash is rejected.

docs.title: Database Migration Policy
docs.text: Database evolution must remain safe across SaaS and customer-hosted deployments, including delayed customer upgrades and application rollback constraints.

docs.title: Principles
docs.text:
• Alembic is the only supported production schema migration path.
  • Schema changes are reviewed like application code.
  • Migrations are repeatable at deployment orchestration level and observable.
  • Destructive removal is delayed until all supported application versions stop using the old structure.
  • Customer-hosted sites must never require ad-hoc manual SQL in a normal release.
  • Migration compatibility is part of the release manifest/support window.

docs.title: Change classes
docs.text: Change Typical approach add nullable column/table/index expand make field mandatory add/backfill/verify, then constrain later rename field/table dual read/write or compatibility view, then contract large backfill resumable/background migration with progress evidence destructive drop final contract release after support window index on large table online/concurrent approach where supported and tested

docs.title: Expand-and-contract
docs.text:
Release N   : add new structure; old application remains compatible
Release N+1 : dual-write/backfill/verify
Release N+2 : switch reads and stop old writes
Release N+3 : remove old structure after supported-version window

docs.title: Migration design requirements
docs.text: Every material migration documents source/target schema versions, expected duration/data volume, lock/availability impact, transaction strategy, backfill/restart behavior, rollback/forward-recovery compatibility, monitoring/progress metric, failure recovery and customer-hosted supported source versions.

docs.title: Long-running migrations
docs.text: Large data backfills should not hold one application deployment/DB transaction indefinitely. Prefer resumable idempotent jobs with checkpoints and verification before enabling a final constraint/contract step.

docs.title: Rollback
docs.text: Application rollback is allowed only when the target older application can safely operate on the migrated schema. If not, the release is declared forward-fix only and deployment/runbook must state that explicitly before Stable promotion.

docs.title: Customer-hosted upgrades
docs.text: Release package declares minimum/maximum supported source app/schema versions. Unsupported jumps are blocked and LMS provides the required intermediate upgrade path rather than attempting an unknown migration.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text: CI/integration tests cover clean install and upgrade from supported baseline. Risky changes additionally test realistic data volume, interruption/restart, rollback compatibility and repeated orchestration invocation.

docs.title: Backup and evidence
docs.text: High-risk migration requires verified backup/recovery readiness. Deployment records source/target schema version, migration IDs, duration, result and failure/recovery actions.

docs.title: Backend Modules — Detailed Responsibilities
docs.text: This page defines the initial modular-monolith boundaries. Modules may share one deployable process and database while maintaining explicit ownership and service interfaces.

docs.title: Identity & Access
docs.text:
Responsibilities: - development username/password authentication - session/token issuance - role and permission evaluation - tenant/customer scope enforcement - future OIDC/SSO adapter boundary

Must not: - own commercial entitlement logic - directly mutate device grants

docs.title: Customer, Site & Topology
docs.text:
Responsibilities: - customer lifecycle - site lifecycle and timezone - device ownership relationships - device-to-site assignments including multi-site server topology - transfer/decommission coordination

Key invariants: - a device has one commercial owner at a time - site assignments are explicit and auditable - transfer never silently overwrites previous ownership

docs.title: Device Enrollment
docs.text:
Responsibilities: - enrollment authorization creation - single-use/short-lived enrollment token validation - public-key registration - fingerprint version validation - duplicate/prior-registration detection - initial hardware inventory capture

Outputs a registered device identity only; registration does not grant paid rights.

docs.title: Catalog
docs.text: Responsibilities: - products - features - dependencies - compatibility metadata - marketplace visibility - release/model associations

docs.title: Entitlements
docs.text:
Responsibilities: - commercial rights - subscription/perpetual term - entitlement pools - update-right policy - ERP synchronization boundary

Entitlements are customer-owned business truth and are not directly executable on a device.

docs.title: Allocation
docs.text:
Responsibilities: - distribute pooled quantities to device/site scopes - validate total quantity - support reallocation - create a stable snapshot used for grant generation

Reallocation affecting multiple devices must be transactionally coordinated.

docs.title: Policy Engine
docs.text:
Responsibilities: - trial duration - offline validity - grace - update rights - co-termination - release-channel eligibility - override hierarchy - maker-checker requirement determination

Resolution hierarchy is explicit and deterministic: platform -> product -> customer/entitlement -> site/device exception where supported.

docs.title: Grant Service
docs.text:
Responsibilities: - construct canonical device-bound grant payload - resolve dependencies and constraints - revision and supersession - signing request - issuance record - delivery/reconciliation state

Signing private-key operations are delegated to the signing boundary.

docs.title: Capacity Service
docs.text:
Responsibilities: - inventory normalization - benchmark lookup - current+proposed workload calculation - feasibility result - recommended alternatives - assessment evidence/versioning

Must never mutate commercial entitlement automatically.

docs.title: Marketplace
docs.text: Responsibilities: - feature discoverability - customer/device eligibility - trial/purchase initiation - capacity preview - current entitlement and release readiness view

docs.title: Release & Artifact Management
docs.text: Responsibilities: - feature/application/UI/runtime releases - release channels - signed manifest metadata - artifact repository references - compatibility/dependency graph - release-set composition

docs.title: Model Management
docs.text: Responsibilities: - model identity/version - encryption metadata - compatibility - model-only OTA - device model inventory reconciliation

docs.title: Deployment Orchestration
docs.text: Responsibilities: - target selection - automatic/manual policy - maintenance-window scheduling - concurrency - per-device state - retry policy - rollback observation - installation receipt reconciliation

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text: Responsibilities: - renewal reminders - commercial renewal workflow - offline check-in freshness - grace/restriction - revocation - rehost - decommission

docs.title: Audit & Notification
docs.text: Audit is append-only for privileged and business-significant events. Notification starts with portal + email and retains an adapter boundary for webhooks.

docs.title: Observability & Initial SLO Baseline
docs.text: Observability must make business-state failures diagnosable across API, background jobs, signing, deployment and edge reconciliation. Metrics are useful only when they map to actionable runbooks and customer impact.

docs.title: Golden signals
docs.text:
• availability
  • latency
  • error rate
  • saturation
  • queue/backlog age and depth
  • dependency health
  • workflow completion/failure rate

docs.title: Proposed service indicators
docs.text:
Capability Indicator Initial engineering target Core LMS API successful non-maintenance requests 99.9% monthly SaaS Read API p95 latency < 500 ms excluding artifact transfer Write API p95 latency < 1 s excluding signing/package generation Signing request p95 under normal load < 2 s Audit append persistence success 99.99% Deployment orchestration state survives restart 100% durable Background jobs oldest normal-priority pending age product/runbook threshold Offline reconciliation unreconciled receipt age visible by policy/site

These are engineering baselines, not contractual SLAs. Business/operations must approve final targets before external commitments.

docs.text:
• request count/latency/status/error code by endpoint/module
  • auth failure/rate limit
  • tenant authorization denial count
  • DB pool/query saturation

docs.text:
• entitlement/allocation/grant mutation success/failure
  • signing pending/failure
  • grant issued/delivered/accepted lag
  • stale check-in and grace/restricted device counts
  • renewal queue and expiry counts

docs.title: Release/deployment

• jobs/targets by state
  • install success/failure/rollback rate
  • rollback failure
  • artifact download/hash/signature failure
  • rollout pause/stop triggers

docs.title: Capacity

• assessment pass/warn/fail/stale
  • benchmark-profile missing/low-confidence
  • reassessment rate
  • local versus central outcome divergence

docs.title: Infrastructure/dependencies
docs.text:
• PostgreSQL health/storage/connections
  • artifact repository latency/error/capacity
  • signing provider latency/error
  • SMTP/ERP/telemetry dependency failures
  • backup age/failure
  • outbox/job queue depth/dead letters

docs.title: Logs
docs.text: Structured JSON logs include UTC timestamp, level, request/correlation ID, module, tenant-safe object IDs, operation, result and stable error code. They exclude passwords, tokens, signing keys, unwrapped model keys and decrypted models.

docs.title: Tracing
docs.text: Trace/correlation context propagates from API through application service, DB/outbox/job, signing/artifact dependency and deployment orchestration where supported. Edge receipts/check-ins carry identifiers that allow cross-boundary correlation even without distributed tracing.

docs.title: Alerting
docs.text: Alerts should be symptom/customer-impact oriented: signing unavailable, DB unavailable, dead-letter growth, rollback failure, backup stale, cross-tenant anomaly, release signature failures or large stale-check-in spike. Every paging alert maps to an owner/runbook.

docs.title: SLO governance
docs.text: Each SLO defines measurement window, exclusions, data source, owner and error-budget response. Targets are revisited after production measurements rather than silently changed to fit observed behavior.

docs.text: Within /v1, additive fields are allowed, removal/semantic repurposing is not. Breaking changes require a new API version or a documented migration window.

docs.text: For workflows such as grant signing, email delivery, ERP reconciliation and deployment dispatch: 1. commit business state and an outbox row in the same database transaction 2. background worker claims the outbox item 3. perform external action 4. persist success/failure and retry metadata 5. emit audit event

docs.text:
Permission checks evaluate: 1. authenticated principal 2. effective permissions 3. customer/product/site/device scope 4. object status and policy 5. maker-checker requirement if sensitive

docs.title: Developer restrictions
docs.text: Developer role may create and test plugins/releases/models only in Development/QA/Internal channels by default. Production Stable/LTS promotion requires Release Manager plus approval gates.

docs.title: Capacity Management
docs.text: Capacity management answers what this hardware can run at the target performance, independently from what the customer commercially owns.

docs.title: Four independent states
docs.text:
A feature/device combination must keep these states separate:

  1. Licensed — commercial right exists.
  2. Compatible — OS/runtime/hardware/dependency requirements are satisfied.
  3. Capacity Validated — combined workload meets the performance target or an approved warning policy.
  4. Installed / Healthy — required application/model components are installed and healthy.

A feature activates only when all required gates pass.

docs.title: Authority model
docs.text:
Central Capacity Engine performs advisory pre-assessment using reported inventory, workload definitions and approved benchmark profiles.

Local Capacity Engine performs the authoritative activation check using current drivers, resources, active streams, installed versions and actual local runtime conditions.

docs.title: Core process
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    A[Collect stable inventory] --> B[Check compatibility]
    B --> C[Describe current + proposed workloads]
    C --> D[Select approved benchmark profiles]
    D --> E[Calculate combined resource budget]
    E --> F[Compare against target/headroom policy]
    F --> G{PASS / WARNING / FAIL}
    G -->|PASS| H[Recommend activation]
    G -->|WARNING| I[Recommend constrained configuration]
    G -->|FAIL| J[Recommend alternatives / hardware change]
    H --> K[Local authoritative recheck]
    I --> K
    J --> K
    K --> L[Monitor runtime and reassess on change]

docs.title: Non-negotiable rules
docs.text:
• Capacity never silently reduces purchased entitlement.
  • Licensed camera/feature quantity is not itself a capacity calculation.
  • Existing and proposed workloads are evaluated together.
  • Central advice may become stale; local activation remains authoritative.
  • Capacity recommendations are explicit and operator-selectable.
  • Benchmark evidence is versioned and governed.
  • Runtime changes can invalidate an old assessment.

docs.title: Authority split
docs.text:
Central Capacity Engine performs advisory pre-assessment using reported inventory and benchmark profiles.

Local Capacity Engine is authoritative for actual activation because it sees current runtime, active streams, drivers, local resources and installed components.

docs.title: Activation gate
docs.text: A feature may activate only when: 1. grant is valid 2. compatibility constraints pass 3. required package/model is installed and healthy 4. local combined-workload capacity validation passes for the selected configuration

docs.title: Recommendation mode
docs.text:
The engine recommends; it does not silently reconfigure commercial use.

Example for licensed People Counting 8 + PPE 4 when full combined workload fails: - PC 8 + PPE 2 - PC 4 + PPE 4 - reduce FPS/resolution - select optimized model/runtime - move one workload to another device - upgrade hardware

The customer/admin explicitly chooses an allowed recommendation. Purchased entitlement remains People Counting 8 + PPE 4 unless a commercial change is separately made.

docs.title: Confidence and evidence
docs.text: Assessment records should include benchmark profile/version, inventory version, workload inputs, result, limiting resource, recommendations and confidence/evidence quality.

docs.title: Benchmark Profile Governance
docs.text: Benchmark data is production engineering evidence. It requires versioning, ownership and release discipline.

docs.title: Benchmark profile dimensions
docs.text: A profile may be keyed by: - hardware class/model - accelerator/GPU architecture and VRAM - driver/runtime stack - feature/model/version - resolution/FPS/codec - decode path - inference backend and precision - concurrent workloads - measured latency/FPS/utilization/headroom

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
DRAFT -> VALIDATING -> APPROVED -> ACTIVE -> SUPERSEDED -> RETIRED

Only APPROVED/ACTIVE benchmark profiles may drive production recommendations.

docs.title: Evidence requirements
docs.text: Each benchmark profile records: - benchmark version - test hardware identity/class - software/runtime versions - test dataset/workload definition - warm-up period - sample duration - measured throughput/latency - CPU/RAM/GPU/VRAM/decode utilization - temperature/throttling observations - target/headroom thresholds - test date and owner - approval status

docs.title: Matching
docs.text: The Capacity Engine chooses the closest valid profile using explicit compatibility rules. It must not silently use a materially different hardware/runtime profile without reducing confidence or marking the result unsupported.

docs.title: Confidence
docs.text: Suggested confidence categories: - high: exact or validated-equivalent profile - medium: approved near-match with bounded interpolation - low: weak match; recommendation only, activation may require local empirical validation - unsupported: no valid evidence

docs.title: Headroom
docs.text:
Capacity results should expose remaining headroom for limiting resources when measurable. Example: GPU compute headroom 14%, VRAM headroom 22%, CPU headroom 35%.

Thresholds are product/benchmark policy, not hard-coded globally.

docs.title: Default decision mode
docs.text: The Capacity Engine recommends a feasible configuration. The customer/admin explicitly selects the configuration. The platform must never silently lower camera count, FPS, resolution or purchased entitlement.

docs.title: PASS
docs.text: Activation may proceed if all licensing, compatibility, installation and health gates also pass.

docs.title: WARNING
docs.text: Activation may proceed only if product policy permits warning acceptance. The selected configuration and warning acknowledgement are audited.

docs.title: FAIL
docs.text: Normal activation is blocked. The system presents recommendations such as reduced active workload, lower FPS/resolution, alternative model/runtime, moving workloads, second device or hardware upgrade.

docs.title: Exceptional override
docs.text:
If the company chooses to support a capacity override for exceptional cases, it is a privileged maker-checker action and must: - never change the commercial entitlement - capture requester, approver, reason and expiry - bind to a specific device/workload/release/model context - be time-limited or revision-limited - generate an audit event - be visible in support/operations views - automatically become invalid when material hardware/runtime/workload state changes

A capacity override must not bypass hard technical incompatibility such as unsupported architecture, missing required runtime or invalid package/model signature.

docs.title: Recommendation selection
docs.text: The selected recommendation becomes part of the activation/deployment record so later support can distinguish licensed rights from the operator-selected active configuration.

docs.title: Inventory & Benchmarking
docs.text: Stable inventory and dynamic resource snapshots are stored separately.

docs.title: Stable inventory
docs.text:
Collect at minimum:

  • CPU model, architecture, physical/logical cores and relevant frequency/capability data
  • RAM total and configured limits
  • GPU model/architecture, VRAM and relevant compute capability
  • accelerators such as Jetson/NPU where applicable
  • storage total/free/filesystem/health evidence
  • OS distribution/version, kernel
  • GPU/accelerator drivers
  • CUDA, TensorRT, DeepStream and product runtime versions
  • camera workload descriptors: count, resolution, FPS, codec/decode requirements
  • installed services, application releases and model inventory

docs.title: Dynamic snapshots
docs.text:
Capture separately:

  • available RAM
  • free disk
  • GPU/accelerator utilization
  • temperature/throttling
  • active streams
  • active workloads
  • other runtime pressure signals needed by the local Capacity Engine

docs.title: Benchmark profiles
docs.text:
Capacity decisions use measured, versioned benchmark profiles across:

  • hardware class
  • analytics model/version
  • resolution
  • FPS
  • inference backend
  • decoder/pipeline
  • concurrent workloads
  • target latency/FPS/SLA

Instantaneous utilization alone is not a benchmark.

Every assessment must record the benchmark profile/version and inventory/workload inputs used so the result can be reproduced and audited.

docs.title: Combined Workload Planning
docs.text:
Capacity planning evaluates the complete active and proposed workload, not individual feature quotas in isolation.

flowchart TD
    A[Collect Inventory] --> B[Compatibility Check]
    B --> C[Load Existing Workloads]
    C --> D[Add Proposed Workload]
    D --> E[Resolve Approved Benchmark Profiles]
    E --> F[Calculate Combined CPU/RAM/GPU/VRAM/Decode/Disk/Thermal Budget]
    F --> G[Apply Performance + Headroom Targets]
    G --> H{PASS / WARNING / FAIL}
    H -->|PASS| I[Recommend Activation]
    H -->|WARNING| J[Recommend Approved Alternatives]
    H -->|FAIL| K[Block Normal Activation + Recommend Alternatives]
    I --> L[Local Authoritative Recheck]
    J --> L
    K --> L

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Commercial entitlement:

People Counting = 8 cameras
PPE = 4 cameras

The Capacity Engine does not assume 8 + 4 = 12 cameras is feasible. It evaluates the real combined workload using model/runtime/resolution/FPS/decode and concurrency evidence.

If the selected workload does not meet target performance, recommendations may include:

  • People Counting 8 + PPE 2
  • People Counting 4 + PPE 4
  • lower FPS
  • lower resolution
  • different decode path
  • optimized model/runtime
  • move a workload to another device
  • deploy a second device
  • hardware upgrade

The operator/customer chooses an allowed configuration. Purchased entitlement remains unchanged.

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
A capacity assessment should return:

  • result: pass / warning / fail / stale
  • limiting resource(s)
  • compatibility blockers
  • benchmark profile/version
  • workload hash/input summary
  • expected/observed headroom
  • confidence/evidence quality
  • recommendations
  • assessment timestamp and freshness
  • whether local revalidation is required

docs.title: Reassessment & Runtime Monitoring
docs.text: Capacity is not a one-time registration result. Assessments become stale when relevant conditions change.

docs.title: Mandatory reassessment triggers
docs.text:
• hardware inventory change
  • GPU/accelerator or driver change
  • CUDA/TensorRT/DeepStream/runtime change
  • application/feature release change
  • model version change
  • camera count/resolution/FPS/codec change
  • new feature activation
  • feature deactivation that changes combined workload
  • site-to-device workload movement
  • benchmark profile superseded by a materially different approved profile
  • repeated runtime degradation or thermal throttling

docs.title: Runtime monitoring signals
docs.text: Where available, monitor: - achieved inference/processed FPS - p95/p99 inference latency - dropped/late frames - CPU/GPU utilization - VRAM/RAM pressure - decoder utilization - temperature/throttling - service health/restarts - active stream count

docs.title: Drift handling
docs.text:
Healthy -> Warning -> Reassess -> Recommendation / Operator Action
                     |
                     +-> Critical degradation -> protect service / fail feature according to runtime safety policy

Runtime degradation does not rewrite entitlement. It may trigger a new capacity assessment and recommendation.

docs.title: Assessment freshness
docs.text: Each assessment records inventory version, resource snapshot timestamp, workload hash, benchmark version and software/model versions. If any required input changes, the previous assessment becomes stale.

docs.title: Central vs local drift
docs.text: Central LMS may show an advisory result based on last reported evidence. The local Capacity Engine remains authoritative for activation because it can detect current real conditions.

docs.title: Telemetry integration
docs.text: Capacity history may be forwarded to telemetry/analytics for trend analysis, but transactional activation state stays in the operational LMS/device state model.

docs.title: Capacity Status Model
docs.text: Capacity-related states must remain separate from commercial licensing and installation state. UI, API and audit records must not collapse them into one boolean.

docs.title: Independent status dimensions
docs.text:
Dimension Meaning Example states Licensed Customer/device has valid commercial authorization not_entitled, entitled, grant_pending, grant_active Compatible Software/model can technically run on this platform/runtime unknown, compatible, incompatible, blocked_dependency Capacity validated Combined workload is expected to meet the defined performance target not_assessed, pass, warning, fail, stale Installed / healthy Required application/model components are present and healthy not_installed, staged, healthy, degraded, failed

These dimensions are evaluated independently and then combined for activation.

docs.title: Activation rule
docs.text:
Licensed
AND Compatible
AND Capacity Validated
AND Installed / Healthy
= Feature may activate

A commercial entitlement can be valid even when the device is incompatible or under-capacity. Capacity failure never removes purchased entitlement.

docs.title: Capacity result semantics
docs.text:
PASS — benchmark evidence and current local conditions meet target with required headroom.

WARNING — workload is likely feasible but headroom/confidence is below preferred target, or the operator must choose an allowed lower-load configuration.

FAIL — the selected combined workload does not meet the minimum activation target.

STALE — the assessment is no longer valid because inventory, runtime, model, workload or benchmark policy changed.

docs.title: Reason-code examples
docs.text:
CAP_GPU_VRAM_INSUFFICIENT
CAP_GPU_COMPUTE_BELOW_TARGET
CAP_CPU_HEADROOM_LOW
CAP_RAM_HEADROOM_LOW
CAP_DISK_FREE_LOW
CAP_RUNTIME_UNSUPPORTED
CAP_DRIVER_MISMATCH
CAP_DECODE_BUDGET_EXCEEDED
CAP_COMBINED_WORKLOAD_EXCEEDS_PROFILE
CAP_BENCHMARK_PROFILE_MISSING
CAP_INVENTORY_STALE
CAP_RESOURCE_SNAPSHOT_STALE

Reason codes are stable machine-readable values and map to operator-safe recommendations.

docs.title: Workload Model
docs.text: Capacity planning is based on actual workload characteristics rather than licensed quantity alone.

docs.title: Workload dimensions
docs.text: A workload profile should capture, where relevant: - feature/capability code - analytics model ID and version - camera/input count - per-input resolution - FPS - codec - decode path (CPU/GPU/hardware decoder) - inference backend - precision - batching/concurrency - preprocessing/postprocessing cost class - retention/output pipeline impact where applicable - site assignment - required performance target such as minimum processed FPS or maximum latency

docs.title: Example workload
docs.text:
{
  "feature_id": "ppe_detection",
  "model_id": "ppe_detector",
  "model_version": "7.3.0",
  "site_id": "site_a",
  "inputs": {
    "camera_count": 4,
    "resolution": "1920x1080",
    "fps": 10,
    "codec": "h264",
    "decode_path": "gpu"
  },
  "runtime": {
    "backend": "tensorrt",
    "precision": "fp16"
  },
  "target": {
    "min_processed_fps": 9.5,
    "max_p95_latency_ms": 250
  }
}

docs.title: Combined workload budget
docs.text:
The Capacity Engine evaluates all active workloads plus the proposed workload together.

Existing workload A
+ Existing workload B
+ Proposed workload C
----------------------
Combined CPU / RAM / GPU / VRAM / decode / storage / thermal budget

Licensed quotas must not simply be added and treated as capacity.

docs.title: Multi-site devices
docs.text: For a device serving multiple sites, the workload model retains site attribution but capacity is evaluated at the shared device resource level. Site limits constrain commercial use; shared hardware capacity constrains actual concurrent execution.

docs.title: Workload identity
docs.text: Persist a stable workload profile or canonical workload hash so assessments can be reproduced and compared over time.

docs.title: Open Decisions
docs.text:
Open decisions are intentional unresolved choices. They must have an owner, decision deadline/milestone and constraints so implementation does not accidentally choose by default.

Topic Status Must be decided before Constraints already fixed Production human authentication / OIDC / SSO / MFA profile Open production security freeze RBAC/scope independent of IdP; privileged MFA target Exact model key wrapping / secure local key storage Security ADR required production model OTA no universal password; protected KMS/HSM boundary; device/deployment authorization Telemetry privacy / opt-in / residency / retention Open production telemetry enablement licensing cannot depend on high-volume telemetry Final generated OpenAPI schemas/error catalogue freeze Open implementation/API freeze /v1, stable error codes, idempotency/scoping rules Enterprise HA topology and RTO/RPO Open enterprise SLA offering Phase 1 backup/recovery required Final release archive/package format Proposed ADR Update Manager implementation freeze signed manifest/artifacts, traditional package, Windows-compatible abstraction Benchmark thresholds/headroom per product/hardware Product/performance decision capacity production activation benchmark profiles versioned; local authority Supported historical-version upgrade window Release/Support decision first production upgrade policy manifest declares supported source versions

docs.title: Governance
docs.text: Each open decision is resolved through ADR/product/operations approval appropriate to its domain. Until resolved, implementation must preserve the documented abstraction instead of hard-coding a choice.

docs.title: Phase Exit Criteria
docs.text: Delivery phases are complete only when their defined outputs and evidence are accepted.

docs.title: Phase 1 — Trust foundation
docs.text: Exit: device identity, enrollment, signed grant canonicalization, verifier, anti-replay/rollback tests and signing-key separation demonstrated.

docs.title: Phase 2 — Registry & licensing
docs.text: Exit: customer/site/device topology, entitlement pools, allocations, grants, base/add-on rules, tenant authorization and audit tests pass.

docs.title: Phase 3 — Capacity
docs.text: Exit: inventory schema, workload model, benchmark governance, central assessment, local authoritative check, recommendations and reassessment triggers validated against representative hardware.

docs.title: Phase 4 — Marketplace & release management
docs.text: Exit: catalog, trial/purchase flow, release channels, signed manifests, artifact repository, dependency/compatibility checks and portal states complete.

docs.title: Phase 5 — Model OTA & deployment
docs.text: Exit: encrypted model delivery, model inventory, auto/manual deployment, maintenance windows, release-set health-check/rollback and model-only OTA proven.

docs.title: Phase 6 — Lifecycle/offline
docs.text: Exit: renewal, three clocks, check-in, grace, revocation, rehost, transfer, decommission, online/offline/air-gapped request-response and receipt reconciliation pass end-to-end tests.

docs.title: Phase 7 — Hardening
docs.text: Exit: VAPT disposition, performance/resilience testing, backup restore, DR exercise, operational runbooks, monitoring/alerting, support readiness, ERP reconciliation and production release approval complete.

docs.title: Ownership
docs.text: Each phase has named Product, Engineering, QA and Security/Operations approvers appropriate to the risk. Evidence is linked to issues/PRs/test reports/releases rather than accepted verbally.

docs.title: Implementation Phases
docs.text: Phases are dependency-ordered capability increments. A phase is not complete because code exists; it must satisfy the corresponding exit criteria and integration evidence.

docs.title: Phase 1 — Trust foundation
docs.text: Device identity/key storage, enrollment authorization, grant canonicalization/signing/verifier, trust-store/key-purpose separation and anti-replay/rollback foundations.

docs.title: Phase 2 — Registry & licensing
docs.text: Customer/site/device topology, RBAC/tenant scope, entitlement pools, allocations, base/add-on grants, audit and online base activation.

docs.title: Phase 3 — Hardware & capacity
docs.text: Stable inventory, dynamic snapshots, workload model, benchmark governance, central advisory assessment, local authoritative assessment and recommendations.

docs.title: Phase 4 — Marketplace & release management
docs.text: Product/feature catalog, trial/purchase request, artifact repository, release channels, signed release manifests, compatibility/dependency metadata and portal flows.

docs.title: Phase 5 — Model OTA & deployment
docs.text: Encrypted model lifecycle, model inventory, release sets, online deployment jobs, AUTO/MANUAL policy, maintenance windows, health-check, rollback and model-only OTA.

docs.title: Phase 6 — Lifecycle & offline
docs.text: Renewal, three clocks, check-in, grace/restriction, revocation, rehost/transfer/decommission, assisted-offline and fully air-gapped request/response/receipt flows.

docs.title: Phase 7 — Hardening & production readiness
docs.text: Production IAM decision, VAPT, supply-chain controls, key rotation/recovery exercise, performance/resilience tests, DR/restore exercise, monitoring/alerts, runbooks/support, ERP reconciliation and production approval.

docs.title: Dependency principle
docs.text: Do not defer edge integration/offline/security to the final phase. Each earlier phase includes the minimum edge, audit, authorization and test work needed to prove its vertical slice. Phase 7 hardens completed capabilities rather than discovering integration for the first time.

docs.title: Edge / Application Engineering
docs.text: The edge is the enforcement and execution boundary. Central LMS decides commercial policy and issues signed state; the edge decides whether that signed state is valid for the actual device, runtime and workload.

docs.title: Core components
docs.text: Component Responsibility Device Identity Agent key lifecycle, fingerprint evidence, enrollment identity Hardware Inventory Agent stable hardware/runtime inventory and dynamic snapshots License Agent signed grant verification and runtime authorization Local Capacity Engine authoritative combined-workload feasibility check Update Manager package/model verification, staging, migration, health and rollback Product Adapter / Analytics Runtime enforce License Agent decisions at actual feature/workload boundaries Offline Exchange signed request/response import/export and receipt queue

docs.text:
flowchart LR
    ID[Device Identity] --> LA[License Agent]
    INV[Inventory / Workload] --> CAP[Local Capacity]
    UM[Update Manager] --> RT[Runtime]
    LA --> RT
    CAP --> RT
    RT --> REC[Receipts / Check-ins]

docs.title: Edge invariants
docs.text:
1. No protected feature executes solely because a UI toggle is enabled.
  2. License Agent authorization is checked at runtime/workload boundaries.
  3. Local capacity is authoritative for activation.
  4. Update Manager is the only component that commits a Release Set.
  5. Invalid/tampered packages never become active.
  6. Central unavailability does not break a still-valid offline authorization.
  7. Anti-replay/revision/trusted-time state survives service restart.
  8. Recovery/import/diagnostic functions remain available where safe when analytics are restricted.

docs.title: Connectivity modes
docs.text: The same edge components support direct online sync, assisted relay and fully air-gapped controlled-media exchange. Transport changes; signature, binding and local verification semantics do not.

docs.title: Platform abstraction
docs.text: Linux is first. Local interfaces, key-storage abstraction, package handlers and service control are designed so Windows-native implementations can be added without changing central licensing semantics.

docs.title: Device Identity & Hardware Change Policy
docs.text: Device identity binds grants, offline requests and lifecycle records to a cryptographic principal while tolerating legitimate hardware maintenance.

docs.title: Identity material
docs.text:
• device-generated asymmetric key pair
  • stable device ID assigned by LMS
  • registered public key + key ID/history
  • versioned weighted hardware fingerprint
  • hardware inventory snapshot
  • MAC/network identifiers as supporting evidence only

docs.title: Enrollment
docs.text:
1. Device generates key pair locally.
  2. Admin/LMS creates short-lived single-use enrollment authorization.
  3. Device submits token, public key, fingerprint, inventory and product context.
  4. Central validates token/customer/product/duplicate identity.
  5. Central binds device ID to customer and key.
  6. Registration audit event is recorded.

Private key does not leave the device during normal enrollment.

docs.title: Fingerprint design
docs.text: Fingerprint implementation is versioned. Inputs are weighted by stability/identity value rather than exact concatenated hash equality. The raw data needed for support/change evaluation is handled according to security/privacy policy.

docs.title: Typical lower-weight/minor changes
docs.text:
• RAM upgrade/replacement
  • storage replacement
  • NIC replacement
  • added accelerator while core identity remains consistent

docs.title: Typical major changes
docs.text:
• motherboard/system identity replacement
  • device private-key loss/recreation
  • multiple core identity attributes change beyond threshold
  • evidence strongly suggests cloning/identity duplication

docs.title: Decision outcome
docs.text:
MATCH -> continue
MINOR_CHANGE -> audit + compatibility/capacity revalidation
MAJOR_CHANGE -> REHOST_REQUIRED
SUSPECT_DUPLICATE -> quarantine/review

docs.title: Key rotation
docs.text: Normal key rotation, if supported, must authenticate with the existing device identity or an approved recovery/rehost workflow and retain key history. A new key must not silently create a second device or inherit rights without validation.

docs.title: Rehost flow
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A[Identity mismatch detected] --> B{Minor / Major / Suspicious}
    B -->|Minor| C[Revalidate compatibility/capacity]
    C --> D[Continue + audit]
    B -->|Major| E[REHOST_REQUIRED]
    B -->|Suspicious| Q[Quarantine / support-security review]
    E --> F[Request + maker-checker approval]
    F --> G[Register replacement identity]
    G --> H[Reconcile allocation + supersede old grant]
    H --> I[Retire old key/binding]

docs.title: Cloning protection
docs.text: Central detects duplicate/contradictory key/fingerprint/customer assignments. Edge grants are bound to registered device identity and revision. MAC spoofing alone cannot satisfy identity.

docs.title: Related SDR
docs.text: SDR-DEV-005 through SDR-DEV-011

docs.title: License Agent
docs.text: The License Agent is the local policy-enforcement authority for licensed runtime features. It validates signed central authorization and exposes an explicit local authorization contract to analytics services.

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
• load and verify signed grants
  • validate trusted key ID/algorithm/canonicalization profile
  • enforce device/product/site binding
  • enforce commercial valid-from/valid-until
  • enforce offline freshness and grace independently
  • enforce revision/supersession/anti-rollback
  • resolve base/add-on dependencies
  • enforce quantity and dynamic constraints
  • use persisted last-known trusted time
  • expose effective feature state/reason codes
  • produce signed acceptance/check-in evidence where required

docs.title: Startup
docs.text: On service startup: 1. load protected local identity/trust state 2. validate persisted grant artifacts 3. reject rollback to a lower accepted revision 4. evaluate trusted-time state 5. publish effective authorization state 6. keep protected analytics disabled until authorization is established

docs.title: Authorization response
docs.text:
{
  "feature_id": "ppe_detection",
  "decision": "allow",
  "grant_id": "grant_1001",
  "revision": 8,
  "effective_limits": {"camera_count": 4},
  "commercial_valid_until": "2027-10-31T23:59:59Z",
  "offline_fresh_until": "2026-10-25T12:00:00Z",
  "reason_codes": []
}

Possible decisions are allow, restricted, and deny. Reasons are machine-readable and safe for support.

docs.title: Runtime enforcement
docs.text: Analytics services ask the License Agent at actual workload creation/change boundaries. A cached allow decision is bounded by grant/time/revision context and must be invalidated when grant/policy state changes.

docs.title: Failure behavior
docs.text: Invalid signature, wrong subject, revoked trust key, stale rollback revision or malformed signed payload fail closed. Central LMS unavailability alone does not immediately fail a still-valid offline grant.

docs.title: Recovery accessibility
docs.text: When license execution is denied, the device should retain access to license import, diagnostics, support status and recovery workflows where product safety allows.

docs.title: Local Component Interfaces
docs.text: Local components must interact through explicit contracts so product teams do not bypass licensing or update controls.

docs.title: License Agent API
docs.text:
Suggested local-only interface:

GET  /local/v1/license/status
POST /local/v1/license/import
POST /local/v1/license/check
GET  /local/v1/features/effective

license/check inputs feature, requested quantity/scope, product context and optional workload reference; output is allow/deny/restricted with reason code and effective grant revision.

docs.title: Capacity Engine API
docs.text:
POST /local/v1/capacity/assess
GET  /local/v1/capacity/latest

Inputs include current resource snapshot, existing workloads, proposed workloads and benchmark profile version. It returns pass/warning/fail plus recommendations; it never changes purchased rights.

docs.title: Update Manager API
docs.text:
POST /local/v1/releases/import
POST /local/v1/releases/install
POST /local/v1/releases/rollback
GET  /local/v1/releases/status
GET  /local/v1/models/inventory

Only the Update Manager may activate a release set. Product services must not unpack arbitrary marketplace files directly.

docs.title: Runtime adapter contract
docs.text: Analytics services must ask the License Agent for authorization at actual execution boundaries. UI state may mirror authorization but cannot be the enforcement layer.

docs.title: Local persistence
docs.text: Protected local state should include accepted grant revision/sequence, last-known trusted time, current release set, rollback release set, installed model inventory and latest signed receipt queue.

docs.title: Offline & Air-Gapped Workflows
docs.text: Offline support is a first-class product path, not an exception.

docs.title: Request package contains
docs.text:
• request_id and nonce
  • device identity/public-key reference
  • current grant revisions
  • installed release/model inventory
  • hardware inventory version and relevant workload
  • requested operation: activation, trial, renewal, release update, model update
  • device signature over canonical request payload

docs.title: Response package contains
docs.text:
• request_id/nonce binding
  • signed grant revision(s) where applicable
  • release-set manifest
  • only required/missing artifacts
  • encrypted model artifacts if required
  • signatures/hashes
  • expiry/import policy

docs.title: Local import order
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A[Read Package] --> B[Verify package signature/hash]
    B --> C[Verify request_id + nonce binding]
    C --> D[Verify device/product scope]
    D --> E[Reject replay / stale revision]
    E --> F[Resolve grant and dependencies]
    F --> G[Capacity re-check]
    G --> H[Stage release set]
    H --> I[Health check]
    I -->|Pass| J[Commit + activate]
    I -->|Fail| K[Rollback]
    J --> L[Generate signed receipt]

Revocation cannot be instantaneous on a fully air-gapped device; it becomes effective when new signed state is imported or when existing offline authorization expires.

docs.title: Release Set & Rollback Contract
docs.text: A deployment is committed as a coherent Release Set, not a collection of independently active files. This prevents application/plugin/model/config combinations that have never been validated together.

docs.title: Release Set content
docs.text:
release_set_id: rs_2026_10_18_01
application: 5.8.0
features:
  ppe: 4.2.1
ui: 2.5.0
runtime: 3.7.0
models:
  ppe_detector: 7.3.0
config_schema: 6
manifest_version: 1

docs.title: Invariants
docs.text:
• one Release Set is Active at a time for a product runtime scope
  • Active points only to a health-validated committed set
  • the immediately previous known-good set is retained
  • every referenced artifact/model is hash/signature verified
  • model/runtime/plugin compatibility is resolved before commit
  • rollback restores compatible config/schema/model state together

docs.title: Update transaction
docs.text:
1. resolve target Release Set and source-version compatibility
  2. preflight license/update rights, dependencies, disk, local capacity and maintenance policy
  3. reserve/preserve previous known-good set
  4. fetch/import only missing verified artifacts
  5. verify manifest and every artifact
  6. stage in non-active location
  7. run signed migration/install handlers
  8. start target services and model warm-up
  9. execute health/readiness probes
  10. atomically switch Active pointer/state
  11. emit installation receipt

docs.title: Rollback transaction
docs.text: Rollback is triggered by failed migration/start/health, automatic rollout policy or authorized operator action. It: 1. stops/isolates failed target services 2. restores previous application/plugin/UI/runtime versions 3. restores compatible model set 4. restores compatible configuration/schema snapshot/path 5. starts previous services 6. validates rollback health 7. records rollback result/receipt

docs.title: Retention
docs.text: Immediately previous known-good Release Set is mandatory. Retain 2–3 known-good sets where disk permits. Cleanup SHALL never delete the only locally known rollback path before a new release is proven healthy.

docs.title: Interrupted install/restart
docs.text: Update state is durable. After process/device restart, Update Manager determines whether it can safely resume staging or must rollback; it must not mark a partially installed set Active merely because files exist.

docs.title: Model-only update
docs.text: A model-only deployment still creates/updates the coherent Release Set identity so support and rollback can reconstruct the exact active combination.

docs.title: Related SDR
docs.text: SDR-OTA-008, SDR-OTA-009, SDR-MOD-006, SDR-MOD-007

docs.title: Runtime Enforcement & Protected Local State
docs.text: License enforcement must occur at the actual service/runtime boundary, not only in portal/UI controls.

docs.title: Authorization decision
docs.text: Before starting or expanding a protected feature, the runtime adapter checks: 1. signed grant validity 2. device/product/site scope 3. grant revision/supersession 4. commercial term 5. offline freshness/grace 6. feature dependencies 7. requested quantity/limits 8. installed release/model compatibility 9. local capacity result 10. runtime health

docs.title: Fail-closed vs recoverability
docs.text: Unauthorized analytics execution fails closed. Recovery functions such as license import, diagnostics and support status should remain accessible where product safety permits.

docs.title: Protected local state
docs.text:
Persist at minimum: - device private-key reference/protected key handle - highest accepted grant revision/sequence - last-known trusted time - current grant set - current and previous known-good release set - installed model inventory - pending signed receipts - latest local capacity assessment/workload hash

State that prevents rollback/replay should use the strongest practical local protection available for the platform.

docs.title: Clock handling
docs.text: A suspicious backward clock jump does not automatically extend rights. The License Agent uses persisted trusted-time evidence and moves to revalidation/restricted behavior according to policy.

docs.title: Runtime quantity enforcement
docs.text: Camera/feature limits are checked when workloads are created/changed, not only at startup. A device serving multiple sites enforces both total device limits and applicable site constraints.

docs.title: Service restart
docs.text: After restart, the runtime reconstructs effective authorization from verified persisted grants and protected monotonic state before enabling protected analytics.

docs.title: Update Manager
docs.text: The Update Manager is the only component allowed to commit application/feature/UI/runtime/model release sets on the edge.

docs.title: Transaction
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A[Receive Deployment / Import Bundle] --> B[Validate Manifest Schema + Signature]
    B --> C[Validate Every Artifact Hash / Signature]
    C --> D[Check OS / Architecture / Runtime Compatibility]
    D --> E[Check License / Update Right]
    E --> F[Check Disk / Dependencies]
    F --> G[Local Capacity Preflight]
    G --> H[Preserve Known-Good Release Set]
    H --> I[Stage to Non-Active Location]
    I --> J[Run Signed Migration / Install Handlers]
    J --> K[Start / Restart Services]
    K --> L[Warm-up + Health Checks]
    L -->|Pass| M[Atomic Commit]
    L -->|Fail| N[Rollback Coherent Release Set]
    M --> O[Signed Installation Receipt]
    N --> O

docs.title: Preflight
docs.text: Validate manifest version, target product/device, OS/architecture, source-version support, config schema, required runtime/model versions, disk space, grant/update rights, maintenance policy and local capacity.

docs.title: Staging and execution
docs.text:
• never execute directly from download/import media
  • stage to dedicated path
  • installation/migration handlers are signed artifacts referenced by manifest
  • preserve previous known-good configuration/model set
  • apply least required privilege
  • make interrupted/restarted execution idempotent/recoverable

docs.title: Health checks
docs.text: Health checks include process/service status plus product-specific readiness/warm-up. Merely starting a process is not a successful deployment.

docs.title: Rollback
docs.text: Rollback restores application, plugins/features, UI/runtime, model versions and compatible configuration as one coherent release set. If rollback itself fails, emit critical failure receipt and require support/incident escalation.

docs.title: Download/import optimization
docs.text: Compare installed artifact/model inventory and fetch/import only missing required content. Existing artifact content is reused only after hash/version validation.

docs.title: Receipt
docs.text: Receipt records device, target release set, previous release set, grant revision, artifact/model versions, result, health outcome, rollback outcome and timestamps.

docs.title: Developer Setup
docs.text: This page defines the local baseline for handbook work and future LMS application development. Exact application commands become executable once the implementation scaffold exists; environment/security rules apply now.

docs.title: Required tools
docs.text:
• Git
  • Python 3.12
  • PostgreSQL client/server or approved local container for development
  • Node.js LTS for React/Vite portal
  • MkDocs dependencies from requirements.txt
  • optional Make/task runner once application scaffold is created

docs.title: Clone and handbook preview
docs.text:
git clone <repository>
cd lms
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate  # Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
mkdocs serve

Documentation changes must pass: 

mkdocs build --strict

docs.title: Local application dependencies
docs.text: When backend implementation begins, local development should provide: - PostgreSQL - development-only signing provider/key - local artifact repository adapter - backend API - worker/scheduler - portal dev server - optional edge simulator/agent

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Use environment/development config files excluded from source control or approved local secret tooling. Never hard-code DB passwords, signing keys, tokens or customer credentials.

docs.title: Data
docs.text: Use synthetic seed data only: customers, sites, devices, entitlements, allocations, grants, capacity profiles, features, releases/models and deployment state. Production exports/backups are prohibited unless formally sanitized/approved.

docs.title: Cryptography
docs.text: Development uses isolated non-production keys. Production KMS/HSM keys and model KEKs are never available in local developer environments.

docs.title: Database workflow
docs.text:
• create schema through Alembic
  • do not manually patch local schema and then forget migration
  • use disposable local DB for destructive development experimentation
  • test upgrade/downgrade/forward compatibility according to migration policy

docs.title: Before PR
docs.text:
• sync/rebase from current main according to team policy
  • run lint/type/unit/integration checks for affected code
  • run migration tests for schema changes
  • run mkdocs build --strict for docs changes
  • verify no secrets/customer data/binary proprietary releases are committed
  • update SDR/ADR/handbook when behavior or architecture changes
  • document rollback/compatibility impact

docs.title: Security hygiene
docs.text: Do not disable certificate/signature/tenant checks in production code paths to make local development easier. Development bypasses, if unavoidable, are explicit environment-scoped implementations that cannot be enabled accidentally in production.

docs.title: Recommended application repository shape
docs.text:
lms/
├── backend/
│   ├── app/
│   ├── migrations/
│   └── tests/
├── portal/
│   ├── src/
│   └── tests/
├── edge/
│   ├── identity/
│   ├── license_agent/
│   ├── capacity/
│   ├── update_manager/
│   └── tests/
├── packaging/
├── scripts/
├── docs/
└── .github/workflows/

The handbook may remain in this repository or a dedicated docs repository, but code ownership and documentation links must remain traceable.

docs.title: Standard local services
docs.text:
• PostgreSQL
  • artifact-storage emulator or local approved filesystem abstraction
  • development signing provider using non-production keys
  • backend API
  • portal dev server
  • optional local edge simulator/test agent

docs.title: Standard commands
docs.text:
Projects should expose consistent commands through Makefile/task runner/scripts, for example:

make setup
make lint
make test
make test-integration
make migrate
make run-backend
make run-portal
make docs
make security-scan

Exact tooling may differ, but CI and developer commands should invoke the same underlying checks.

docs.title: Seed data
docs.text: Development seed data should include synthetic customers, sites, devices, entitlements, grants, capacity profiles, marketplace features and release/model metadata so critical flows can be exercised locally without production data.

docs.title: Engineering Change Control
docs.text: Change control provides traceability and proportionate review without turning every edit into the same process. The required controls depend on what business/security boundary a change affects.

docs.title: Change classes
docs.text: Class Examples Minimum controls Standard bug fix, docs correction, internal refactor PR, tests, qualified review Architecture new module, trust boundary, persistence model, deployment topology SDR/ADR impact review, architecture approval, PR/tests Security-sensitive auth/RBAC, signing, offline parser, model protection, secret handling security review, negative tests, scan/VAPT scope review Commercial-policy entitlement, allocation, trial, renewal, expiry/grace, transfer Product/Commercial approval, regression tests, audit impact Release/OTA manifest, package, migration, rollback, channel behavior Release/Edge review, upgrade/rollback evidence Data migration destructive/backfill/tenant ownership changes migration plan, backup/recovery, performance/locking review Emergency critical security/production correction expedited approver path + full post-change review

docs.title: Required traceability
docs.text:
A material production change is traceable through: 

Requirement / incident / issue
        ↓
SDR + ADR impact
        ↓
PR / review
        ↓
CI / security / test evidence
        ↓
Release identifier / manifest
        ↓
Deployment / migration / audit event
        ↓
Post-release validation

docs.title: Pre-change assessment
docs.text: Every material PR identifies: - affected customers/tenants/modules - API/schema/state-machine impact - security/trust boundary impact - online/offline behavior - migration/upgrade/rollback requirement - capacity/model/release compatibility impact - observability/runbook changes - whether customer communication is required

docs.title: Approval separation
docs.text: Requesters must not self-approve actions where maker-checker or security/release separation is mandated. Code review is not automatically equivalent to commercial/security approval.

docs.title: Emergency changes
docs.text: Emergency does not mean uncontrolled. Minimum requirements are: 1. incident/change owner 2. scoped risk statement 3. at least one authorized approver appropriate to severity 4. test/smoke evidence practical for the emergency 5. rollback/containment plan 6. audit trail 7. post-change review and normal documentation/ADR update

docs.title: Prohibited changes
docs.text:
• direct untracked production DB edits as routine workflow
  • bypassing signing/tenant authorization to restore service
  • replacing published immutable release artifacts in place
  • changing a commercial term/grant without auditable business workflow
  • silently changing Approved ADR behavior inside an unrelated implementation PR

docs.title: Post-change validation
docs.text: Validate release health, tenant isolation, audit events, migration correctness, deployment/rollback status and any affected operational alerts. Failed validation triggers rollback/forward recovery according to release plan.

docs.title: Data Classification & Handling
docs.text: Classification determines where LMS information may be stored, logged, exported and shared. Classification applies to documents, database fields, logs, backups, support bundles and offline packages.

docs.title: Classes
docs.text: Class Examples Handling baseline Public approved public product material externally shareable after publication approval Internal architecture, roadmaps, non-customer operational metrics company/internal authorized access Confidential customer/device inventories, entitlement details, audit exports, deployment metadata need-to-know, scoped access, encrypted transport/storage controls Highly Restricted signing private keys, passwords/tokens, model content keys, security incident secrets dedicated protected systems; never normal docs/logs/tickets

docs.title: Default classification examples
docs.text:
• customer/site/device topology: Confidential
  • entitlement/allocation/grant metadata: Confidential
  • signed grant artifact: Confidential unless product policy classifies differently
  • audit/security export: Confidential
  • source architecture handbook: Internal
  • model binary/IP: Confidential or Highly Restricted according to owner policy
  • private signing key / KEK / unwrapped DEK: Highly Restricted
  • authentication token/password: Highly Restricted

docs.title: Storage rules
docs.text:
Highly Restricted key/credential material is stored only in approved key/secret systems and is never copied into PostgreSQL business tables, documentation or ordinary support archives.

Confidential data in PostgreSQL/artifact storage/backups uses deployment-appropriate access control and encryption-at-rest capabilities.

docs.title: Logging
docs.text: Logs prefer identifiers/references over full payloads. Highly Restricted values are always redacted. Confidential payload details are logged only when explicitly justified in an approved secure diagnostic path.

docs.title: Export and support bundles
docs.text: Exports enforce tenant/object scope. Sensitive global exports may require privileged approval. Support bundles must minimize data and exclude secrets/private keys/decrypted model material.

docs.title: Lower-environment data
docs.text: Production customer data/backups are not copied into development/QA by default. Any approved lower-environment use requires sanitization/anonymization appropriate to classification.

docs.title: Retention/deletion
docs.text: Retention follows audit/business/compliance policy by data class. Legal/security hold overrides normal deletion. Backup copies follow their own managed retention lifecycle.

docs.title: Incident rule
docs.text: Suspected unauthorized disclosure of Confidential or Highly Restricted information triggers security incident triage according to impact and scope.

docs.title: Engineering Decision Gates
docs.text: Decision gates prevent unresolved product/security assumptions from moving invisibly into implementation and production. Evidence is linked to issues/PRs/test reports/releases rather than captured only in meetings.

docs.title: Gate 0 — Problem / Sponsor
docs.text:
Required outputs: - business problem/outcome - sponsor/product owner - scope/non-goals - success measures - affected product/customer classes

Exit condition: problem is worth solving and scope is approved.

docs.title: Gate 1 — Architecture Ready
docs.text:
Required outputs: - relevant SDR requirements - system context/trust boundary impact - state machine and invariants - data ownership/transaction boundaries - central/edge/offline behavior - API/event/local interface draft - ADR created/superseded for durable decisions - threat/capacity/release implications

Exit condition: engineering is not expected to invent architecture while coding.

docs.title: Gate 2 — Development Ready
docs.text:
Required outputs: - decomposed work items - acceptance criteria - owner/dependencies - test approach - migration/upgrade strategy - environments/fixtures/hardware needed - operational/audit/observability expectations

Exit condition: Definition of Ready satisfied.

docs.title: Gate 3 — Release Candidate
docs.text:
Required evidence: - code review merged - CI/integration/security tests - schema migration result - supported upgrade path - rollback/recovery result - tenant-isolation evidence - package/manifest integrity - capacity/model compatibility evidence where affected - documentation current

Exit condition: build is technically eligible for production approval.

docs.title: Gate 4 — Production Approval
docs.text:
Required evidence: - QA acceptance - security/VAPT disposition - release notes/known issues - rollout/canary/concurrency plan - stop/rollback triggers - support/runbook readiness - backup/recovery impact - required maker-checker approvals

Exit condition: Stable promotion/deployment authorized.

docs.title: Gate 5 — Post-Release
docs.text:
Review: - deployment/rollback health - SLO/error/backlog signals - customer/support incidents - security anomalies - unresolved follow-up items - performance/capacity regressions - whether release/ADR/runbook corrections are needed

Exit condition: release is accepted into normal operation or corrective actions are assigned.

docs.title: Gate ownership
docs.text: Product owns problem/business gates; Architecture/Engineering owns design readiness; QA/Security/Release own production evidence; Operations owns recovery/monitoring readiness. High-risk changes require all relevant owners, not one blanket approver.

docs.title: Branching model
docs.text:
Use short-lived branches from main. main must remain releasable/documentation-buildable. Long-lived feature branches are discouraged.

Suggested naming:

feature/<ticket>-short-name
fix/<ticket>-short-name
security/<ticket>-short-name
docs/<ticket>-short-name

docs.title: Pull request requirements
docs.text: Every PR contains: - problem/business context - implementation summary - affected modules - API/schema/migration impact - security impact - test evidence - rollback/compatibility notes where applicable - documentation/ADR updates

docs.title: Review rules
docs.text: At least one qualified reviewer for normal changes. Sensitive areas require an additional domain reviewer: - authentication/RBAC/signing/offline parser -> Security - entitlement/grant/policy -> Backend architecture/product owner - release/update/model OTA -> Release/Edge owner - DB migration -> Backend/data owner

docs.title: Merge policy
docs.text: Prefer squash or rebase according to repository setting, but final history must retain ticket/PR traceability. Direct commits to protected main should be disabled once team development begins.

docs.title: Commit content policy
docs.text: No secrets, private keys, customer exports, production credentials, decrypted model artifacts or proprietary binary releases should be committed to the documentation/source repository.

docs.title: Handbook Status, Authority & Ownership
docs.text: This handbook is the normative internal engineering baseline for LMS unless superseded by a newer approved ADR, formal product/security decision or generated implementation contract explicitly identified as authoritative.

docs.title: Status taxonomy
docs.text:
• Approved — normative implementation baseline
  • Proposed — recommended design awaiting approval
  • Open Decision — constraints are known; implementation must preserve flexibility
  • Superseded — historical decision replaced by another identified record
  • Deprecated — retained for history but must not be used for new implementation
  • Phase 2 / Deferred — intentionally not part of current delivery scope

docs.title: Authority order
docs.text:
When documents conflict, use this order unless a record explicitly states otherwise: 1. approved ADR for durable architecture choice 2. approved SDR/business rule for required behavior 3. generated/frozen API/schema contract for implementation details 4. detailed domain handbook section 5. examples/illustrations

A conflict must be corrected; teams should not silently choose whichever page is convenient.

docs.title: Change ownership
docs.text: Section Primary approver Required co-review when applicable Product/business rules Product/leadership Architecture/QA SDR / Architecture Architecture/Tech Lead Product/Security/Edge ADRs Architecture owner domain owner + Security for trust changes Licensing/grants Backend + Product Security/Edge Capacity Performance/AI + Architecture Edge/Product Marketplace/OTA Product + Release Edge/Security/QA Edge enforcement/update Edge Lead Security/Backend/QA Security/crypto Security Architecture/DevOps/Edge Backend/data/API Backend Lead Security/QA QA/release gates QA/Release Manager domain owner/Security Operations/DR DevOps/Operations Security/Backend

docs.title: Required maintenance
docs.text: A change that modifies observable behavior, business rule, API/event schema, persistent model, trust boundary, release/package format, local edge contract, operational recovery or security control updates the affected handbook/SDR/ADR in the same PR.

docs.title: Review cadence
docs.text:
• release-affecting sections reviewed during release readiness
  • security/DR/runbooks reviewed after incidents/material architecture changes
  • open decisions reviewed at the milestone/deadline recorded in their owning document
  • stale examples/defaults corrected when product policy changes

docs.title: Historical integrity
docs.text: Approved ADRs are historical records; material reversal uses supersession instead of silently rewriting the past decision. Other handbook pages may be edited in place but must preserve change traceability through Git.

docs.title: Content quality rule
docs.text: A page is not considered complete because it exists. Completion requires enough detail to implement, test and operate the behavior or an explicit link to the authoritative detailed specification.

docs.title: Team RACI
docs.text: Area Primary Owner Key contributors / accountability Customer/site/device registry Backend Product, QA Entitlements, allocations & grants Backend Product/Commercial, Security, QA Trial/subscription/perpetual/add-on policy Product/Commercial Backend, QA, Support Renewal/grace/offline-freshness policy Product/Commercial Backend, Support, QA License Agent/runtime enforcement Edge/Application Backend, Security Device identity/key storage Edge/Application Security, Backend Capacity benchmark matrix AI/ML Performance Edge, Backend, QA Capacity engine/recommendations AI/ML Performance + Backend/Edge Product, QA Marketplace Backend/Web Product, Edge, QA Release/OTA orchestration Backend + Edge QA, DevOps, Security Model OTA AI/ML + Edge Backend, Security, QA Signing/key custody DevOps/Security Backend Artifact repository DevOps/Backend Release Manager, Security Release promotion Release Manager / QA Engineering, Security, Product as needed ERP integration Backend Finance/Commercial, Product Notifications/support workflows Backend/Support Product Backup/DR/monitoring DevOps/Operations Backend, Security VAPT Security All engineering teams Handbook/ADRs Architecture/Tech Leads All contributors

docs.title: Approval rule
docs.text: Normal allocations within an approved entitlement may be single-admin or automated. Sensitive actions such as entitlement increase, large custom/perpetual grants, trial extension, forced LTS, major rehost, security/capacity override and signing-key changes use maker-checker approval.

docs.title: Release Approval SOP
docs.text: This SOP governs promotion into production-capable channels.

docs.title: Roles
docs.text:
• Developer: produces Development/QA artifacts
  • QA: validates functional/integration/regression evidence
  • Security: validates security gates for applicable changes
  • Release Manager: owns promotion and rollout
  • Product/Architecture: approves material compatibility/policy impact when needed

docs.title: Promotion path
docs.text: Development -> QA -> Internal/Beta -> Stable -> LTS (explicit)

docs.title: Stable promotion evidence
docs.text: The promotion record references: - source commit/tag - build identity - signed release manifest - automated test report - upgrade/migration test - rollback test - compatibility matrix - capacity/benchmark impact if relevant - security scan/VAPT disposition - release notes - known issues and rollback trigger

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Stable promotion uses maker-checker: Release Manager requests; required QA/Security approver confirms evidence. Same actor must not self-approve when policy requires separation.

docs.title: LTS
docs.text: LTS is never automatic. Company explicitly designates an eligible Stable release as LTS after stability evidence and support-life decision.

docs.title: Emergency release
docs.text: Emergency releases may use an expedited path but still require source traceability, approval, signed artifacts, rollback plan and post-release review within the defined incident process.

docs.title: Audit conclusion
docs.text:
The handbook previously had real omissions in lifecycle state machines, required sequences, portal information architecture, trial eligibility, renewal milestones, device transfer/replacement, relay security, capacity authority, detailed inventory, artifact storage and several security threat details.

Future handbook reviews should use this page as a regression checklist: if a design changes one of these requirements, the corresponding detailed page and this audit must be updated in the same PR.

docs.title: Section-by-Section Content Audit
docs.text: This audit is based on reading the actual handbook content, not counting files or headings. A section is marked Complete only when its core business rules, implementation contract, security/error behavior, tests and operations are materially documented or explicitly linked.

docs.text: The earlier audit overstated completion in several areas. In particular, Security, Backend, Edge, QA, Operations, Telemetry and Architecture had pages whose titles existed but whose content was too thin. This audit intentionally distinguishes Complete baseline, Substantial, and unresolved implementation/open-decision work instead of equating a file's existence with coverage.
