docs.text:
1. production OIDC/SSO/MFA provider/profile
  2. exact model encryption key hierarchy/wrapping/local secure storage
  3. final release archive/package execution format
  4. product-specific benchmark/headroom thresholds and hardware matrix
  5. telemetry privacy/residency/retention commercial policy
  6. enterprise HA topology and contractual RTO/RPO
  7. generated OpenAPI and final physical DDL/index tuning
  8. final UI visual/accessibility design system
  9. product/version support lifetime policy

These are explicit decisions or implementation artifacts; they must not be hidden by calling the handbook 'fully complete'.

docs.title: Engineering & Documentation Standards
docs.text: These standards define the minimum implementation discipline for LMS. Module-specific standards may be stricter.

docs.title: Code
docs.text:
• Python 3.12 baseline for backend/central services unless superseded by ADR
  • typed Python for public/module boundaries and non-trivial domain code
  • Pydantic at external/API/event boundaries
  • SQLAlchemy/Alembic for persistence/migrations
  • explicit domain/application/repository separation where it improves ownership/testability
  • no hidden cross-module database writes
  • deterministic IDs/time handling through shared primitives
  • UTC persistence; site timezone only for display/scheduling interpretation

docs.title: API and contracts
docs.text:
• /v1 versioned API baseline
  • stable machine-readable error codes
  • request/correlation IDs
  • idempotency on retryable writes
  • cursor/bounded pagination for large collections
  • backward compatibility within major version
  • generated OpenAPI becomes executable contract once implementation begins

docs.title: Database
docs.text:
• migrations through Alembic only
  • FK/unique/check constraints enforce invariants where possible
  • optimistic concurrency for mutable aggregates
  • transactional business invariants
  • expand-and-contract for destructive evolution
  • query/index decisions validated against production-like plans before launch

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• deny-by-default authorization
  • tenant/object scope validation server-side
  • no secrets/private keys in source
  • approved crypto libraries only
  • signed/package parsers fail closed
  • sensitive logs redacted
  • threat/negative tests for trust boundaries

docs.title: Reliability
docs.text:
• external side effects use durable outbox/jobs where atomic DB participation is impossible
  • consumers/actions are idempotent
  • retries are bounded and observable
  • dead-letter state is visible and recoverable
  • no silent data correction for commercial truth mismatches

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
• unit + integration + contract + security negative tests as appropriate
  • tenant isolation is release blocking
  • migration/upgrade/rollback tests for release-impacting changes
  • representative edge hardware validation for capacity/update changes

docs.title: Observability
docs.text:
• structured logs
  • metrics for latency/error/saturation/backlog
  • request IDs across API/job/audit flows
  • alerts map to operational runbooks

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
• behavior-changing PR updates handbook in same PR
  • SDR requirements updated when normative behavior changes
  • material architecture changes require ADR
  • statuses Approved/Proposed/Open Decision/Superseded are explicit
  • examples use synthetic data
  • diagrams use maintainable Mermaid where practical

docs.title: Pull-request quality
docs.text: A PR explains problem, affected SDR/ADR, implementation, API/schema/migration impact, security/tenant impact, test evidence, rollback/compatibility and documentation changes.

docs.title: Prohibited shortcuts
docs.text:
• production secrets in source/docs
  • UI-only authorization
  • manual DB schema changes as normal release procedure
  • unsigned executable update content
  • customer-specific hard-coded feature columns
  • swallowing background-job/deployment failures without state/audit evidence

docs.title: ERP Integration Contract
docs.text: ERP and LMS remain separate systems. Integration is intentionally narrow so the LMS does not become an accounting platform.

docs.title: Authority split
docs.text: Data System of record Invoice/payment state ERP Contract/order reference ERP Commercial SKU/order line ERP Customer operational device/site topology LMS Entitlement operational state LMS after approved import Allocation/grant state LMS Deployment/check-in state LMS

docs.title: Inbound ERP event example
docs.text:
{
  "event_id": "erp_evt_001",
  "event_type": "order_line_approved",
  "occurred_at": "2026-10-18T10:00:00Z",
  "customer_external_ref": "CUST-1007",
  "contract_ref": "CTR-2031",
  "order_ref": "SO-9001",
  "line": {
    "product_code": "ANALYTICS_BASE",
    "feature_code": "PPE",
    "quantity": 40,
    "term": {"type": "subscription", "start": "2026-11-01", "end": "2027-10-31"}
  }
}

docs.title: Integration rules
docs.text:
• ERP events are idempotent by event_id.
  • Unknown product/SKU mapping is quarantined for review.
  • Payment/renewal status alone does not directly modify a device grant; LMS first updates entitlement state and then issues a new grant revision.
  • ERP retries are safe.
  • LMS never overwrites financial truth back into ERP unless a separate outbound contract explicitly permits it.

docs.title: Reconciliation
docs.text: A scheduled reconciliation compares approved ERP commercial lines against LMS entitlements. Differences are categorized as missing, extra, quantity mismatch, term mismatch or mapping failure and surfaced to operations without destructive auto-correction.

docs.title: Licensing Architecture
docs.text: Licensing separates commercial ownership from runtime execution. A device is not authorized because it is registered, because a customer paid, or because a package is installed; it is authorized only when the required signed grant and runtime conditions are valid.

docs.title: Core model
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    E[Customer Entitlement] --> A[Allocation]
    A --> G[Device-bound Signed Grant]
    G --> V[Local Verification]
    V --> C[Dependency / Time / Capacity Checks]
    C --> R[Runtime Permission]

docs.title: Domain responsibilities
docs.text: Concept Meaning System of record Entitlement What the customer commercially owns LMS commercial state Allocation How pooled rights are distributed LMS licensing state Grant Signed executable authorization LMS issued artifact + edge accepted state Effective runtime right What the device may execute now Edge License Agent

docs.title: Required distinctions
docs.text:
• registration != licensing
  • licensing != capacity
  • payment/renewal approval != accepted device authorization
  • marketplace purchase/trial request != executable permission
  • installed package != licensed feature

docs.title: Supported commercial forms
docs.text:
• subscription base
  • perpetual base
  • co-terminating subscription add-on
  • explicitly independent add-on
  • perpetual base with subscription add-on
  • policy-configurable trial
  • pooled quantities reallocated between devices/sites

docs.title: Lifecycle invariants
docs.text:
1. Active allocations never exceed purchased/approved entitlement quantity.
  2. Replacement grants supersede prior revisions; old/new rights cannot remain indefinitely additive.
  3. Commercial expiry, offline freshness and grace remain separate clocks.
  4. Check-in never extends paid commercial expiry.
  5. Offline renewal becomes active only after local receipt and acceptance.
  6. Dependent add-ons become dormant when their required base is inactive unless explicitly independent.

docs.title: Security model
docs.text: Grants are device-bound, digitally signed and verified locally. Devices persist anti-rollback state and reject stale revisions. Signing private keys remain in the protected signing boundary.

docs.title: Failure behavior
docs.text: Central LMS outage does not immediately invalidate a still-valid offline grant. Invalid signature, wrong device binding, expired term, stale revision or violated dependency fails authorization according to policy. Recovery/diagnostics remain available where safe.

docs.title: Related SDR
docs.text: SDR-LIC-*, SDR-TRL-*, SDR-LIF-*

docs.title: Transfer between customer/site ownership contexts
docs.text:
1. Create transfer request with current owner/site, requested owner/site, reason and effective intent.
  2. Validate caller authority and affected entitlements/allocations.
  3. Require approval according to policy; cross-customer transfer is always sensitive.
  4. Freeze or supersede grants that would become invalid under the new ownership.
  5. Update ownership/site assignments only after approval.
  6. Issue new grants under the valid target entitlement context.
  7. Reconcile old allocations and audit before/after ownership.

Silent overwrite of owner/site is prohibited.

docs.title: Replacement device
docs.text: For device replacement: - register replacement identity as a new device - approve replacement/rehost relationship - return or reassign allocation from retired device - issue new device-bound grant - retire old device/grant binding - preserve audit lineage between old and replacement devices

docs.title: Rehost
docs.text: Rehost is used when the physical system is intended to remain the same commercial installation but cryptographic/major hardware identity changed. Major motherboard/key changes enter REHOST_REQUIRED until approved.

docs.title: Revocation
docs.text:
Connected device: central revocation/superseding state is delivered at next sync/check-in according to policy.

Air-gapped device: immediate remote revocation is impossible. Revocation becomes effective after importing signed updated state or when current offline authorization expires.

docs.title: Diagnostics in grace/restricted state
docs.text: Where product safety permits, grace/restricted mode should preserve access to diagnostics, license recovery/import, support status and existing customer data. Expired commercial rights should disable unauthorized analytics execution, not make recovery impossible.

docs.title: Entitlements & Allocations
docs.text:
Example entitlement: PPE = 40 camera rights.

Device A = 16
Device B = 12
Device C = 8
Unallocated = 4

The customer/admin may redistribute rights without a new purchase while total allocation stays within the purchased pool.

docs.title: Reallocation controls
docs.text:
1. Validate total allocation.
  2. Calculate affected device grants.
  3. Issue superseding revisions.
  4. Prevent temporary double-allocation beyond approved transition policy.
  5. Synchronize online or through offline package.
  6. Audit before/after values and actor.

docs.title: Customer, device and site scope
docs.text:
A device is commercially owned by one customer but may serve multiple sites through explicit device-site assignments.

A device-bound grant may contain site-specific limits. Example:

{
  "device_id": "dev_x",
  "capability": "ppe_detection",
  "site_limits": [
    {"site_id": "site_a", "max_cameras": 4},
    {"site_id": "site_b", "max_cameras": 8}
  ]
}

The grant remains bound to the device, while constraints may partition the permitted quantity by site.

docs.title: Allocation invariant
docs.text:
For every entitlement item:

sum(active allocations) <= purchased/approved entitlement quantity

Reallocation must preserve this invariant transactionally and must not rely on UI-only validation.

docs.title: Signed Grant Canonical Format
docs.text: The signed grant is a device-verifiable authorization artifact. The final binary/serialization format is implementation-specific, but signing semantics must be deterministic.

docs.title: Canonical payload example
docs.text:
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "grant_id": "grant_001",
  "revision": 8,
  "supersedes": "grant_000",
  "issued_at": "2026-10-18T12:00:00Z",
  "subject": {
    "customer_id": "cust_001",
    "product_id": "analytics",
    "device_id": "dev_001"
  },
  "capabilities": [
    {
      "code": "ppe_detection",
      "limits": [{"key": "camera_count", "op": "lte", "value": 4}],
      "dependencies": [{"capability": "analytics_base", "required": true}]
    }
  ],
  "commercial": {"type": "subscription", "valid_until": "2027-10-31T23:59:59Z"},
  "runtime": {"offline_days": 7, "grace_days": 7},
  "key_id": "lic_sign_01"
}

docs.title: Signing requirements
docs.text:
1. Remove the signature field from the payload.
  2. Normalize field order/encoding using a documented canonicalization method.
  3. Hash/sign the canonical bytes using the active license-signing key.
  4. Attach key_id, algorithm and signature.
  5. Device reconstructs the same canonical bytes before verification.

docs.title: Anti-rollback
docs.text: Device persists the highest accepted revision/sequence per relevant grant lineage and rejects older revisions unless an explicit signed recovery mechanism exists.

docs.title: Key rotation
docs.text: Verification trust store may contain current and retiring public keys. New grants use only the active key; older valid grants remain verifiable during the planned rotation window.

docs.title: Device-Bound Grants
docs.text: A grant is the signed executable permission derived from approved entitlement, allocation and resolved policy. It is not the commercial contract itself.

docs.title: Required grant content
docs.text: A production grant carries at minimum: - schema/canonicalization version - grant ID and revision - superseded grant lineage - issue timestamp - customer/product/device subject - one or more capabilities - quantity/site/model/runtime constraints - commercial term - offline freshness and grace policy - dependencies - update-right policy where applicable - signing key ID/algorithm - signature

docs.title: Illustrative grant
docs.text:
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "grant_id": "grant_1001",
  "revision": 8,
  "supersedes": "grant_0988",
  "subject": {
    "customer_id": "cust_100",
    "product_id": "ai_box",
    "device_id": "dev_310"
  },
  "capabilities": [{
    "code": "ppe_detection",
    "limits": [{"key": "camera_count", "op": "lte", "value": 4}],
    "dependencies": [{"capability": "analytics_base", "required": true}]
  }],
  "commercial": {"type": "subscription", "valid_until": "2027-10-31T23:59:59Z"},
  "runtime": {"offline_days": 7, "grace_days": 7},
  "key_id": "lic_sign_01",
  "algorithm": "ed25519",
  "signature": "base64..."
}

docs.title: Issuance rules
docs.text:
Grant issuance SHALL: 1. resolve current entitlement/allocation/policy 2. validate tenant/device ownership 3. validate pooled quantity invariant 4. calculate revision/supersession 5. persist issuance intent and audit state 6. obtain signature from protected signing service 7. persist signed artifact metadata 8. deliver online or through offline response flow

Direct client-provided limits are not trusted without policy/entitlement validation.

docs.title: Acceptance rules
docs.text: Edge accepts a grant only after verifying: - trusted key ID and signature - canonical payload integrity - customer/product/device binding - valid-from/valid-until - revision and supersession - dependency constraints - current trusted time - local quantity/site scope - relevant compatibility/capacity/install state

docs.title: Supersession
docs.text: Replacement grant revisions SHALL not be aggregated with superseded versions. Edge persists the highest accepted revision per lineage and rejects rollback unless an explicit signed recovery mechanism exists.

docs.title: Delivery state
docs.text: Issued, Delivered/Imported and Accepted/Active are separate states. Central issuance alone is not evidence that an offline device is using the new rights.

docs.title: Perpetual/update rights
docs.text: Perpetual grants can carry explicit update-right policies such as unlimited, during_active_term, remaining_major_updates, until_version or none.

docs.title: Failure handling
docs.text: Signing failure leaves issuance pending/retryable through durable jobs/outbox. Invalid or rejected grants never replace a previously valid accepted grant unless policy explicitly transitions the device to restricted state.

docs.title: Related SDR
docs.text: SDR-LIC-004 through SDR-LIC-011

docs.title: Dynamic License Policy Model
docs.text: The licensing model is generic and data-driven. New features/products should normally be onboarded through catalog/policy/constraint metadata rather than adding feature-specific schema columns or hard-coded licensing branches.

docs.title: Grant policy inputs
docs.text: Effective grant policy is derived from: - product/feature catalog definition - customer entitlement item - allocation - term type and dates - product/customer/site/device policy hierarchy - trial/campaign rules - base/add-on dependencies - update-right policy - approved exceptions/overrides

docs.title: Generic grant shape
docs.text: A grant contains: - subject: customer/product/device and optional site constraints - capability code - grant type: base/add-on/trial/subscription/perpetual - constraints - commercial validity - offline/grace policy - revision/supersession - dependencies - update-right policy - policy/source revisions - signature metadata

docs.title: Constraint model
docs.text:
[
  {"key": "camera_count", "op": "lte", "value": 8},
  {"key": "site_id", "op": "in", "value": ["site_a", "site_b"]},
  {"key": "model_family", "op": "in", "value": ["ppe_v7"]}
]

Supported operators/types are allowlisted/versioned. Unknown security-critical constraint operators are rejected rather than ignored.

docs.title: Constraint resolution
docs.text: Constraints from entitlement/allocation/policy are combined conservatively: lower-scope configuration cannot expand commercial quantity beyond the entitlement/allocation; security minima cannot be relaxed by ordinary policy override.

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text: A capability may require base capabilities/grants. Dependency state is evaluated at runtime; a dependent add-on becomes dormant when required base authorization is inactive unless product policy explicitly marks it independent.

docs.title: Update rights
docs.text:
{
  "mode": "remaining_major_updates",
  "remaining_updates": 1,
  "until_version": null
}

Supported modes include unlimited, during_active_term, remaining_major_updates, until_version, and none. Update Manager checks update rights separately from feature execution rights.

docs.title: Trials
docs.text: Trial policy adds eligibility, activation-start behavior and duration but still produces a normal signed time-limited grant. Trial state is not a special UI-only boolean.

docs.title: Policy snapshot/audit
docs.text: Grant issuance records the relevant resolved policy/source revisions so support can explain why a grant was produced. Sensitive override source/approval is auditable.

docs.title: Extensibility rule
docs.text: Adding a new feature quantity type should require a registered constraint schema/validator and runtime enforcement support; it should not require new feature_x_enabled DB columns.

docs.title: Related SDR
docs.text: SDR-LIC-005, SDR-LIC-006, SDR-LIC-010, SDR-TRL-*

docs.title: Renewal & Offline Validity
docs.text:
Three clocks remain independent:

  1. Commercial term/expiry.
  2. Offline authorization freshness — default 7 days unless overridden by policy.
  3. Grace/restriction period — default 7 days unless separately overridden.

A successful check-in never extends the paid commercial term.

A payment or central entitlement renewal does not activate an offline device until the new signed grant revision is delivered/imported and accepted locally.

docs.title: Reminder baseline
docs.text:
Default proposed reminders are 30 days, 7 days and 1 day before expiry, configurable by product/customer policy.

flowchart LR
    A[Due Soon / Reminder] --> B[Renewal Requested]
    B --> C[Commercial Approval]
    C --> D[Entitlement Term Updated]
    D --> E[New Signed Grant Revision]
    E --> F{Delivery}
    F -->|Online| G[Delivered]
    F -->|Offline| H[Export / Import]
    G --> I[Local Verify]
    H --> I
    I --> J[Atomic Accept / Active]
    J --> K[Receipt / Reconciliation]

docs.title: Status milestones
docs.text:
• Due Soon
  • Requested
  • Approved / Grant Issued
  • Delivered / Imported
  • Accepted / Active
  • Failed / Rejected
  • Expired / Restricted

Issued != Delivered != Accepted.

If delivery or verification fails, the old grant continues according to its own expiry/grace rules. Where product safety permits, restricted/grace mode should preserve diagnostics, license recovery/import and access to existing customer data while unauthorized analytics execution is disabled.

docs.title: Trials
docs.text:
• Default trial period is 7 days.
  • Duration is policy/campaign configurable by feature, product or approved customer exception.
  • Trial starts at first successful feature activation, not request, issuance, package download or import.
  • Trial is a signed time-limited device-bound grant, not a UI flag.
  • Baseline eligibility is one trial per customer entitlement + feature.
  • Admin/campaign override may permit extension or an additional trial, but the override is auditable and may require maker-checker approval.
  • Globally reusable trial licenses are prohibited.

docs.title: Add-ons
docs.text:
Subscription add-ons normally co-terminate with the active base subscription.

Base: Jan 1 ---------------- Dec 31
PPE:                 Sep 1 -- Dec 31
Renewal: Jan 1 ---- Base + PPE together

Commercial pricing may be prorated for the remaining base term. An explicitly independent add-on may carry its own term when product/commercial policy permits it.

Perpetual base licenses may have subscription add-ons.

Dependent add-ons become dormant when their required base is inactive unless the add-on policy explicitly marks them independent.

docs.title: Purchase/activation distinction
docs.text: A trial request, purchase request, payment approval or marketplace selection does not itself authorize runtime execution. The device still requires a valid signed grant and all compatibility/capacity/install/health gates.

docs.title: Marketplace & OTA Architecture
docs.text: Marketplace and OTA are different responsibilities inside one LMS. Marketplace determines what may be discovered/requested; OTA determines how approved compatible content is safely delivered and activated.

docs.title: Capability split
docs.text:
Marketplace OTA feature discovery release/model resolution eligibility/trial/purchase request deployment target selection commercial/catalog metadata download/offline bundle generation entitlement/capacity preview signature/hash verification request/approval status install/health/rollback

Neither side alone authorizes runtime execution. Final activation requires valid grant + compatibility + installed healthy content + local capacity approval.

docs.title: End-to-end flow
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    A[Discover Feature] --> B[Compatibility / Capacity Preview]
    B --> C[Trial or Purchase Request]
    C --> D[Commercial / Policy Approval]
    D --> E[Signed Grant]
    E --> F[Resolve Release Set]
    F --> G[Online or Offline Delivery]
    G --> H[Verify + Stage]
    H --> I[Local Capacity + Health]
    I --> J[Commit / Rollback]
    J --> K[Runtime Enable + Receipt]

docs.title: Release principles
docs.text:
• Stable is default for automatic production deployment
  • LTS is explicitly designated
  • published artifacts/manifests are immutable
  • application and models are independently versioned
  • coherent Release Set governs compatibility and rollback
  • delta/minimal transfer avoids re-downloading verified local content
  • offline and online use the same artifact trust model

docs.title: Failure semantics
docs.text: Purchase success does not imply installation. Download success does not imply activation. Install without health success does not become Active. Failed deployment preserves/returns to known-good release state.

docs.title: Related SDR
docs.text: SDR-MKT-*, SDR-OTA-*, SDR-MOD-*

docs.title: Deployment Job State Machine
docs.text: Deployment orchestration must be restart-safe and deterministic.

docs.title: Job states
docs.text:
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Draft
    Draft --> Scheduled
    Scheduled --> Running
    Running --> Completed
    Running --> PartiallyFailed
    Running --> Failed
    Scheduled --> Cancelled
    Running --> Cancelling
    Cancelling --> Cancelled

docs.title: Target states
docs.text:
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Pending
    Pending --> WaitingWindow
    WaitingWindow --> Preflight
    Preflight --> Downloading
    Downloading --> Verifying
    Verifying --> Staging
    Staging --> Installing
    Installing --> HealthCheck
    HealthCheck --> Active
    HealthCheck --> RollingBack
    RollingBack --> RolledBack
    Preflight --> Blocked
    Verifying --> Failed
    Installing --> Failed

docs.title: Retry policy
docs.text:
• Network/artifact transient failures may retry with exponential backoff.
  • Signature/hash/compatibility failures are non-retryable until input changes.
  • Installation failure triggers rollback before retry consideration.
  • Automatic mode obeys maintenance window and concurrency limits.
  • Manual mode requires explicit deployment approval/start.

docs.title: Completion semantics
docs.text: A job is Completed only when every target reaches Active or an explicitly accepted terminal exclusion state. PartiallyFailed preserves successful targets and clearly reports failed/rolled-back targets.

docs.title: Deployment & Rollback
docs.text: Deployment turns an approved release set into per-device installation actions with policy, maintenance-window, concurrency, health and rollback controls.

docs.title: Policy hierarchy
docs.text:
Platform Default -> Product -> Customer -> Site -> Device Override

Supported settings include AUTO/MANUAL, channel, maintenance window, model-only OTA, application OTA, concurrency, rollout batch size and auto-rollback.

Default automatic maintenance window: 01:00–03:00 in site timezone, customer configurable.

docs.title: Target resolution
docs.text: Before scheduling, LMS resolves target customer/site/device ownership, entitlement/update rights, device status, compatible release-set path and maintenance policy. A target that becomes ineligible before install is revalidated and blocked.

docs.title: Rollout strategies
docs.text:
• all-at-once only for explicitly accepted small/low-risk scope
  • batch/concurrency-limited rollout
  • canary/pilot subset before broader rollout where risk warrants
  • pause/stop on configured failure threshold
  • forced rollout requires privileged approval when policy marks it sensitive

docs.title: Per-target execution
docs.text:
Pending -> Waiting Window -> Preflight -> Download/Import -> Verify -> Stage -> Install -> Health Check -> Active
                                                              |
                                                              +-> Rollback -> Rolled Back

docs.title: Preflight gates
docs.text:
• release/channel eligibility
  • current/source version supported
  • grant/update right valid
  • OS/architecture/runtime compatible
  • dependencies/model versions resolvable
  • disk space and rollback reserve
  • local capacity check
  • package/trust-store compatibility

docs.title: Success semantics
docs.text: A target is successful only after health check and atomic commit. Downloaded or installed files alone do not mean Active.

docs.title: Rollback
docs.text: Rollback restores a coherent release set, not one binary. Keep 2–3 known-good releases when disk permits; the immediately previous known-good set is mandatory.

docs.title: Automatic stop criteria
docs.text: Systemic signature/hash failure, repeated migration failure, rollback failure, or failure-rate threshold should stop/pause further rollout and alert Release/Operations.

docs.title: Offline deployment
docs.text: Air-gapped deployment uses the same target/release semantics. The response bundle carries required release-set artifacts; final central state becomes authoritative only after signed installation receipt reconciliation.

docs.title: Model Manifest Schema
docs.text: Model metadata is independent from application releases so compatible model-only OTA does not force application redownload.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
{
  "manifest_version": 1,
  "model_release_id": "mr_ppe_7_3_0",
  "model_id": "ppe_detector",
  "version": "7.3.0",
  "channel": "stable",
  "framework": "TensorRT",
  "precision": "FP16",
  "input": {"width": 640, "height": 640},
  "compatibility": {
    "architectures": ["x86_64"],
    "gpu_families": ["nvidia"],
    "runtime": ">=3.7 <4.0",
    "feature_release": ">=4.2 <5.0"
  },
  "artifact": {
    "uri_ref": "artifact://models/ppe/7.3.0",
    "sha256": "...",
    "encrypted": true,
    "encryption_profile": "model-envelope-v1",
    "size": 901234567
  },
  "validation": {
    "warmup_required": true,
    "expected_output_schema": 3
  },
  "signature": {"key_id": "release_sign_01", "algorithm": "Ed25519", "value": "..."}
}

docs.title: Key handling principle
docs.text: The repository stores encrypted model material. Entitlement controls permission to use the model; device authorization controls decryption. A universal embedded model password is prohibited.

docs.title: Model OTA
docs.text: AI models are first-class managed artifacts with independent identity, versioning, compatibility, encryption, deployment and rollback.

docs.title: Model release metadata
docs.text: Each release records model ID/version, framework/backend, precision, input/output schema, feature compatibility, runtime range, accelerator/hardware compatibility, encrypted content hash, size, release channel and signing/encryption profile.

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A[Create Model Release] --> B[Validate Metadata / Compatibility]
    B --> C[Encrypt Artifact with DEK]
    C --> D[Sign Manifest / Artifact]
    D --> E[Publish to Channel]
    E --> F[Resolve Authorized Target]
    F --> G[Compatibility + Capacity Check]
    G --> H[Download / Import Missing Content]
    H --> I[Verify Signature + Hash]
    I --> J[Authorize / Unwrap Content Key]
    J --> K[Stage Model]
    K --> L[Warm-up / Functional Health Check]
    L -->|Pass| M[Atomic Activate]
    L -->|Fail| N[Restore Previous Model]

docs.title: Independent OTA
docs.text: A compatible model-only release may deploy without application redownload. The manifest must declare compatible feature/runtime ranges, and local inventory prevents redundant download.

docs.title: Authorization and encryption
docs.text: Possessing the encrypted model file is not sufficient for use. The device needs both valid entitlement/grant authorization and authorized content-key unwrap/use according to the security model.

docs.title: Rollback
docs.text: Previous known-good model remains available when storage permits. If application/plugin and model versions are tightly coupled, they are deployed/rolled back as one Release Set.

docs.title: Inventory
docs.text: Edge reports model ID/version/hash/status. Central uses inventory for delta bundle generation and support visibility.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text: Health/warm-up is model-specific and may include load success, inference sanity, expected output schema and latency/performance threshold. A hash-valid model that fails warm-up is not activated.

docs.title: Security boundary
docs.text: No universal model password is permitted. Exact key wrapping/local secure storage follows ADR-009.

docs.title: Release Manifest Schema
docs.text: The release manifest is the machine-readable contract between Release Management and the edge Update Manager. It is signed and immutable after publication.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
{
  "manifest_version": 1,
  "release_id": "rel_ppe_4_2_1",
  "feature_id": "ppe_detection",
  "version": "4.2.1",
  "channel": "stable",
  "platforms": [
    {"os": "ubuntu", "versions": ["22.04", "24.04"], "arch": ["x86_64", "aarch64"]}
  ],
  "requirements": {
    "runtime": ">=3.7 <4.0",
    "disk_free_mb": 2500,
    "ram_mb": 8192
  },
  "artifacts": [
    {
      "artifact_id": "art_app_421",
      "type": "application",
      "version": "4.2.1",
      "sha256": "...",
      "size": 123456789
    }
  ],
  "models": [
    {"model_id": "ppe_detector", "version_range": ">=7.3 <8.0", "required": true}
  ],
  "migrations": {
    "config_schema_from": [4,5],
    "config_schema_to": 6,
    "automatic": true
  },
  "health_checks": [
    {"type": "http", "target": "http://127.0.0.1:9000/health", "timeout_sec": 30}
  ],
  "rollback": {"supported": true, "minimum_free_mb": 3000},
  "signature": {"key_id": "release_sign_01", "algorithm": "Ed25519", "value": "..."}
}

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• Manifest canonicalization is defined before signing.
  • Artifact hash is mandatory.
  • Dependencies use explicit version ranges.
  • Installation scripts are treated as signed artifacts, never unsigned inline commands.
  • A published manifest is immutable; corrections create a new release/version.
  • Device must reject unsupported manifest versions.

docs.title: Release Management
docs.text: Release Management governs creation, evidence, promotion, retirement and supportability of application, feature/plugin, UI/runtime and model-compatible releases.

docs.title: Channels
docs.text:
Development -> QA -> Internal/Beta -> Stable -> LTS -> Retired

Channel movement is a controlled promotion, not a file copy.

docs.title: Channel semantics
docs.text:
Channel Purpose Production eligible Development developer iteration No QA formal test candidate No Internal/Beta controlled non-general validation Restricted Stable default production release Yes LTS explicitly designated long-support release Yes Retired blocked from new deployment No

Automatic production updates consume Stable by default. LTS targeting is explicitly controlled by the company.

docs.title: Release evidence
docs.text: Before Stable promotion, the release record links to: - source commit/tag - CI/build identity - release manifest and artifact hashes - automated unit/integration/upgrade tests - migration result - rollback result - compatibility matrix - capacity/benchmark impact where relevant - security scan/VAPT disposition - SBOM/provenance record - release notes/known issues - rollout and rollback triggers

docs.title: Publication
docs.text: Published manifests/artifacts are immutable. Correction creates a new release/version. Artifact repository content alone does not make a release deployable; release state and approval govern eligibility.

docs.title: Traditional package standard
docs.text:
release/
├── manifest.json
├── application/
├── ui/
├── migrations/
├── configs/
├── dependencies/
├── install/
│   ├── install.sh
│   ├── rollback.sh
│   └── healthcheck.sh
└── signature

Install/migration/rollback handlers are signed artifacts. No normal production release depends on manual site migration.

docs.title: Retirement
docs.text: Retirement prevents new deployment. Existing installations are not silently removed. Support policy determines required upgrade path and emergency-block behavior.

docs.title: LTS
docs.text: LTS designation requires explicit support-life decision, supported upgrade paths, compatibility evidence and operational commitment. Stable does not automatically become LTS.

docs.title: Versioning & Compatibility Policy
docs.text: Versioning is a contract between central LMS, edge components, release packages and models. A version string alone is insufficient; every release declares what it can safely run with and upgrade from.

docs.title: Version domains
docs.text:
• LMS central application/API
  • edge application
  • feature/plugin
  • local component/interface
  • manifest/package schema
  • configuration schema
  • model
  • grant schema/canonicalization
  • offline request/response schema

Semantic Versioning is preferred for software interfaces where practical, but compatibility declarations are authoritative.

docs.title: Release compatibility declaration
docs.text: Every deployable release declares: - product - OS/version + architecture - supported source application versions - runtime/framework ranges - feature/plugin dependency ranges - model ID/version ranges - config schema range/target - required manifest/local interface versions - minimum hardware/runtime prerequisites - migration path - rollback compatibility

docs.title: Compatibility result
docs.text:
COMPATIBLE
INCOMPATIBLE
UPGRADE_PATH_REQUIRED
UNKNOWN / UNSUPPORTED

Unknown is not treated as compatible for automatic production deployment.

docs.title: Upgrade paths
docs.text: Release manifests explicitly declare supported source versions. If a customer is too old for a direct jump, LMS/Update Manager identifies the required intermediate release rather than attempting an unsupported migration.

docs.title: Breaking changes
docs.text: Breaking local API, manifest, offline protocol or grant schema changes require: 1. version/schema bump 2. compatibility/migration plan 3. staged/dual-read strategy where needed 4. support-window communication 5. old/new contract tests 6. rollback/forward-recovery validation

docs.title: Model compatibility
docs.text: Models are independently versioned and declare compatible feature/runtime/hardware ranges. Model-only OTA is permitted only when these constraints and local capacity/health checks pass.

docs.title: Central-edge compatibility
docs.text: Central LMS must remain able to serve supported historical edge versions during their declared support window. APIs/offline package builders should not assume all devices upgrade simultaneously.

docs.title: Retirement/support window
docs.text: The organization must finalize how many historical application versions remain supported. Until then, every release explicitly declares source/support compatibility; no code path assumes indefinite backward compatibility.

docs.title: Related SDR
docs.text: SDR-OTA-006 through SDR-OTA-010, SDR-MOD-006, SDR-BE-006

docs.title: Backup & Recovery
docs.text: Backup/recovery protects business truth, deployment evidence and artifact availability without treating signing private keys as normal application data.

docs.title: Backup scope
docs.text:
• PostgreSQL transactional state
  • audit data
  • artifact metadata and release/model manifests
  • artifact repository binaries or replicated/versioned equivalent
  • deployment/configuration reconstruction metadata
  • operational configuration templates that do not contain raw secrets

Signing private keys use a separate KMS/HSM/provider recovery mechanism and are never copied into ordinary DB/file backups.

docs.title: SaaS Phase 1 baseline
docs.text:
• automated encrypted database backups
  • point-in-time recovery where chosen PostgreSQL platform supports it
  • object/artifact versioning or protected backup
  • backup job monitoring/alerting
  • documented restore procedure
  • regular restore exercise
  • single-primary acceptable initially while remaining HA-ready

docs.title: Customer-hosted baseline
docs.text: Installation package defines what the customer must back up, supported backup commands/provider integration, required artifact/config directories and restore ordering.

docs.title: Restore order
docs.text:
1. establish clean supported LMS environment
  2. restore PostgreSQL
  3. restore/attach artifact repository
  4. restore non-secret configuration/reconstruction metadata
  5. reconnect protected signing provider using its independent process
  6. run integrity/migration compatibility validation
  7. verify tenant/authz/audit state
  8. verify device check-in and safe signing integration

docs.title: Integrity checks
docs.text: Restore validation checks DB consistency, schema version, artifact hashes, manifest availability, audit continuity, application startup and tenant scoping.

docs.title: Recovery evidence
docs.text: Record backup identifier/time, recovery point, operator, restore duration, verification checks, exceptions and remediation.

docs.title: Open decision
docs.text: Exact contractual RPO/RTO remains an enterprise operations decision. Engineering must measure restore performance before any promise is made.

docs.title: Backup Retention & Restore Validation
docs.text: Backup policy must balance recovery, audit/compliance obligations, storage cost and customer-hosted operating constraints. Retention values are deployment policy, but backup classes and validation behavior are mandatory.

docs.title: Backup classes
docs.text: Class Content Protection Transactional DB customers/devices/entitlements/grants/deployments/config metadata encrypted automated backup/PITR where supported Audit append-only audit/security records protected backup/archive Artifact repository release/model binaries + immutable metadata references versioning/replication/backup Reconstruction config deployment/application configuration excluding raw secrets config management/protected backup Secrets/certificates app/service credentials secret-manager/provider recovery Signing keys license/release/model key hierarchy KMS/HSM/provider-specific protected recovery only

docs.title: Retention baseline capability
docs.text:
Implementation SHALL support daily/weekly/monthly tiers and policy-specific extensions. Exact periods are finalized by operations/compliance/customer contract; the software/runbooks must not hard-code one universal retention duration.

Audit retention has its own configured policy (baseline 1–3 years) and is not implicitly equal to DB backup retention.

docs.title: Immutability/protection
docs.text: Where available, critical backups use versioning/object lock/immutable backup controls appropriate to ransomware risk. Backup administrative access is separated from normal application credentials.

docs.title: Restore validation
docs.text: A backup is not considered reliable until restore is tested. Exercises verify: - DB integrity/schema compatibility - tenant/customer ownership paths - grant/allocation/audit continuity - artifact hashes/manifests - application startup/readiness - secret/signing provider reconnection - device check-in and safe signing in test scope - worker/outbox duplicate safety

docs.title: Failure handling
docs.text: Backup failure or stale backup age triggers operations alert. Failed restore exercise creates tracked remediation and may block production-readiness/DR claims.

docs.title: Evidence
docs.text: Record backup ID/time/type, encryption/protection status, selected recovery point, restore environment, duration, validation checks, exceptions and remediation owner.

docs.title: Deletion
docs.text: Expired backups are deleted through managed retention policy. Legal/security incident hold overrides normal deletion where formally applied.

docs.title: Customer-Hosted Deployment Topology
docs.text: Customer-hosted LMS uses the same core application/domain codebase as SaaS, with provider adapters and environment-specific infrastructure.

docs.title: Baseline topology
docs.text:
flowchart TB
    U[Customer/Vendor Admin Browser] --> RP[Reverse Proxy / TLS]
    RP --> LMS[LMS Application / Workers]
    LMS --> PG[(PostgreSQL)]
    LMS --> AR[(Artifact Repository / MinIO or approved storage)]
    LMS --> SG[Signing Gateway / Protected Provider]
    LMS --> SMTP[SMTP / Notification Relay]
    LMS --> OBS[Logs / Metrics Export]
    EDGE[Edge Devices] <--> RP

docs.title: Required components
docs.text:
• TLS termination/reverse proxy or equivalent
  • persistent PostgreSQL
  • persistent artifact repository
  • LMS application + durable background workers/scheduler
  • protected signing provider integration
  • secrets/configuration mechanism
  • backup destination
  • monitoring/log export
  • time synchronization
  • email relay if notifications enabled

docs.title: Network/port principle
docs.text: Only required interfaces are exposed. PostgreSQL/artifact/signing internal endpoints should not be publicly reachable. Edge devices connect to the approved LMS/reverse-proxy endpoint. Exact port/firewall matrix is generated by deployment packaging and security profile.

docs.title: Identity
docs.text: Human authentication may integrate with customer IdP after ADR-008 is resolved. Device authentication remains cryptographic and independent of customer human SSO.

docs.title: Storage
docs.text: PostgreSQL stores transactional metadata; large binaries use MinIO/approved local repository. Backup/restore covers both. Raw signing private keys are outside ordinary storage/backup.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: Initial deployment package validates OS/runtime prerequisites, DB connectivity/schema, artifact storage, signing provider, time and required certificates before marking LMS ready.

docs.title: Upgrade
docs.text: Customer-hosted LMS self-update is manual initially: 1. validate supported source version 2. obtain signed LMS package 3. take verified backup 4. verify package signature 5. run automated migration/update 6. health-check API/workers/dependencies 7. validate safe device check-in/signing 8. record upgrade evidence

docs.title: Failure/recovery
docs.text: Customer-hosted recovery follows backup/DR runbooks. Unsafe DB downgrade is prohibited; release declares rollback versus forward-fix compatibility.

docs.title: HA
docs.text: HA is an enterprise option rather than mandatory Phase 1. Exact app/DB/storage/load-balancer topology and RTO/RPO are deployment-tier decisions; business/domain behavior remains unchanged.

docs.title: Security
docs.text: Customer-hosted does not mean trusted-by-default. Tenant checks, signing separation, audit, secret handling, package verification and least-privilege requirements still apply.

docs.title: Disaster Recovery & Continuity
docs.text: Disaster recovery restores the control plane and its trust relationships without creating a second uncontrolled source of commercial/signing truth.

docs.title: Failure domains
docs.text: DR planning covers: - PostgreSQL loss/corruption - LMS application/infrastructure loss - artifact repository loss/corruption - audit storage loss - signing provider outage/region loss - customer-hosted server loss - credential/certificate loss - ransomware/security incident requiring clean recovery

docs.title: Recovery dependencies
docs.text: Component Recovery source Special constraint PostgreSQL encrypted backups/PITR where supported restore schema/business consistency Artifact repository versioning/replication/protected backup verify hashes after restore Audit data protected backup/archive preserve append-only evidence/identity LMS config reconstruction/config management secrets restored separately Signing metadata PostgreSQL/config private keys are separate Signing private keys KMS/HSM/provider recovery never ordinary file/DB backup Customer-hosted LMS customer backup + signed install package validate supported source/target versions

docs.title: Recovery order
docs.text:
1. establish clean trusted infrastructure
  2. restore database to selected recovery point
  3. restore/attach artifact repository
  4. restore non-secret configuration
  5. restore/reconnect secrets and certificates through protected process
  6. recover/reconnect signing provider independently
  7. verify hashes/audit/schema/tenant authorization
  8. start LMS read paths
  9. validate signing using safe test scope
  10. resume background jobs/outbox after duplicate/idempotency review
  11. allow device check-ins/deployments
  12. monitor reconciliation/backlog and communicate recovery status

docs.title: Recovery safety
docs.text:
• do not replay side effects blindly after DB restore
  • inspect outbox/job states versus external systems
  • ERP reconciliation detects commercial divergence
  • devices may have accepted grant/release state newer than the restored central point; check-in/receipt reconciliation must handle this explicitly
  • compromised signing key recovery follows security incident procedure, not normal DR

docs.title: RTO/RPO
docs.text: Exact contractual enterprise RTO/RPO remain an open business/operations decision. Engineering SHALL measure database restore, artifact recovery, application restart, signing reconnection and reconciliation time before an SLA is promised.

docs.title: Mandatory exercises
docs.text:
• scheduled DB restore
  • full LMS reconstruction
  • artifact integrity verification
  • schema migration + restored-data compatibility
  • signing-provider recovery exercise without exposing raw private keys
  • customer-hosted restore rehearsal
  • worker/outbox duplicate-safety after recovery
  • tabletop security/ransomware clean-room recovery

docs.title: DR evidence
docs.text: Record scenario, recovery point, start/end time, measured data loss, component timings, validation checks, manual steps, failures and corrective owners.

docs.title: Environment classes
docs.text: Environment Purpose Data rule Release channels Local Dev developer iteration synthetic only Development Integration service/edge integration synthetic/test Development/QA QA formal validation synthetic/anonymized QA/Internal Staging production-like readiness anonymized/approved Internal/Stable candidate Production customer service real customer data Stable/LTS only

docs.title: Separation requirements
docs.text:
• Separate credentials and secrets per environment.
  • Production signing keys are never available in lower environments.
  • Development/QA artifacts cannot be promoted implicitly into production; promotion creates explicit approved release state.
  • Test tenants/devices are clearly marked.
  • Production backups are not restored into lower environments without approved sanitization.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Configuration is supplied through environment/secret manager/deployment configuration, never hard-coded. Environment-specific settings include DB connection, artifact storage, signing provider, email provider, telemetry endpoints and auth mode.

docs.title: Time
docs.text: All servers use reliable time synchronization. Persist timestamps in UTC. Site timezone is used for display and maintenance-window interpretation.

docs.title: Incident Response
docs.text: Incident response covers security events and operational failures that materially affect licensing, tenant isolation, deployment, model protection or customer availability.

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text: Detect -> Triage -> Classify -> Contain -> Preserve Evidence -> Recover -> Validate -> Communicate -> Post-Incident Review

docs.title: Immediate evidence
docs.text: Preserve: - request/correlation IDs - security/audit events - affected tenant/customer/device IDs - deployment job/target history - relevant application/security/edge logs - artifact/release hashes and manifest IDs - grant revisions - signing/trust key IDs (never raw private key material) - timestamps and operator actions - relevant approval records

docs.title: Containment rule
docs.text: Containment must avoid destroying evidence or making unsafe commercial changes. Do not bypass signature/tenant controls merely to restore service.

docs.title: Suspected signing-key compromise
docs.text:
1. stop new signing with affected key
  2. identify signed grants/releases and potential exposure window
  3. activate approved replacement key where available
  4. distribute trust-bundle update through supported routes
  5. assess air-gapped devices that cannot receive immediate trust changes
  6. supersede/revoke affected artifacts/grants where policy requires
  7. validate restored signing and initiate post-incident review

docs.title: Tenant-isolation incident
docs.text:
1. treat as security-critical until disproven
  2. restrict risky support/global access paths
  3. preserve request/query/audit evidence
  4. identify data read/write exposure and affected tenants
  5. remediate authorization/query defect
  6. add regression tests before reopening path
  7. follow legal/customer notification policy where applicable

docs.title: Artifact repository compromise / tampered release
docs.text:
1. stop affected deployments
  2. block suspect release/artifact identities
  3. verify signed manifest/content hashes from trusted build evidence
  4. rotate repository credentials if compromised
  5. rebuild/re-publish as a new release if needed
  6. inspect devices that received suspect content
  7. use rollback where active release is unsafe

docs.title: Model key / wrapping compromise
docs.text:
1. disable affected wrapping/master-key path
  2. identify model releases and wrapped-key scopes
  3. rotate KEK/wrapping configuration using approved provider process
  4. regenerate wrapped keys/release metadata as required
  5. assess offline devices unable to receive replacement authorization
  6. document IP/data exposure assessment

docs.title: Compromised human credential / privileged account
docs.text:
1. revoke sessions/tokens
  2. disable/reset identity through IdP/auth system
  3. review privileged actions/audit exports
  4. rotate any derived secrets exposed by the account
  5. restore access using approved identity recovery
  6. review role assignments and strengthen controls if needed

docs.title: Widespread bad release
docs.text:
1. stop/pause rollout
  2. mark release blocked
  3. rollback to known-good release set
  4. verify rollback health receipts
  5. preserve failed installation evidence
  6. communicate affected customers according to incident policy

docs.title: Malicious/malformed offline package exploit attempt
docs.text:
1. quarantine media/package
  2. preserve package hash and parser error evidence
  3. determine whether parsing occurred before signature verification
  4. block/revoke package/request identity as appropriate
  5. patch parser and add regression/fuzz case
  6. inspect similarly exposed devices

docs.title: Communications
docs.text: External communications contain confirmed impact, affected scope and recovery guidance only. Unvalidated technical hypotheses and sensitive security details remain internal until approved.

docs.title: Closure criteria
docs.text: Incident is closed only after containment, recovery validation, evidence retention, customer/internal communications, root-cause analysis, corrective actions with owners and regression/monitoring improvements are documented.

docs.title: SaaS deployment
docs.text:
1. Confirm release approval and backup/recovery readiness.
  2. Apply DB-compatible release using controlled deployment.
  3. Run migrations before/with application start according to migration contract.
  4. Verify API, DB, signing, artifact repository, notification and background-job health.
  5. Run smoke tests for login, device check-in, grant issuance in safe test scope and artifact access.
  6. Monitor errors/latency/queues after release.
  7. Roll back application when safe; do not blindly downgrade incompatible schema.

docs.title: Customer-hosted deployment
docs.text:
1. Validate supported source LMS version and environment prerequisites.
  2. Take verified backup of DB/artifact/config state.
  3. Verify signed vendor LMS package.
  4. Stop/coordinate services according to maintenance procedure.
  5. Execute automated application/migration package.
  6. Run health checks.
  7. Validate customer portal, device check-in and artifact/signing integration.
  8. Complete upgrade receipt/runbook record.

docs.title: Failure handling
docs.text: If migration/app startup fails, follow the release-specific recovery path. Never hand-edit production schema unless an approved emergency procedure explicitly requires it and captures the exact changes.

docs.title: Rollback decision
docs.text: Rollback feasibility is declared by the release. When DB migration is backward-compatible, application rollback may proceed. When not, use forward-fix/recovery procedure rather than unsafe schema downgrade.

docs.title: Post-deployment evidence
docs.text: Record release ID, operator, start/end time, source/target versions, migration result, health result, exceptions and rollback status.

docs.title: Monitoring & Operational Integration
docs.text: ERP contract details live in the Integrations section. This page defines operational monitoring responsibilities.

docs.title: Core health
docs.text: Monitor: - LMS API availability, latency and error rate - PostgreSQL connection/replication/storage health as applicable - background-job queue depth and oldest age - outbox pending/dead-letter count - signing-provider latency/failures - artifact repository latency/errors/capacity - authentication failure/rate-limit anomalies - notification delivery failures - backup success/age - deployment success/failure/rollback rate - device check-in freshness distribution - renewal/trial processing backlog - capacity assessment warning/fail/stale rate - ERP reconciliation mismatch/failure

docs.title: Alert classes
docs.text: Condition Example action API unavailable/high error Operations incident triage Signing unavailable Stop manual retries; queue issuance; escalate if customer impact Dead-letter growth inspect worker/dependency; replay only with approved procedure Backup stale/failed immediate operations investigation Rollback failure high-severity release incident Tenant/authz anomaly security escalation Check-in stale spike connectivity/systemic device investigation ERP mismatch spike integration/commercial reconciliation

docs.title: Dashboards
docs.text: Minimum production dashboards cover API/service health, DB/dependencies, signing, deployments, jobs/outbox, licensing lifecycle, capacity and backup status.

docs.title: Logging and correlation
docs.text: Central logs are structured and include request/correlation ID, tenant-safe object identifiers and stable error codes. Sensitive values remain redacted.

docs.title: ERP monitoring boundary
docs.text: ERP may be authoritative for orders/invoice/payment/contracts. LMS remains authoritative for operational entitlements, allocations, grants, activation, deployment and local acceptance. Integration failure is visible and reconciled; it does not silently rewrite either system.

docs.title: Notification Events & Templates
docs.text: Phase 1 channels are portal + email. The event model must allow webhooks later without changing business modules.

docs.title: Notification event catalogue
docs.text: Event Default audience Urgency renewal_due_30d Customer Admin, Vendor account owner normal renewal_due_7d Customer Admin, Vendor account owner high renewal_due_1d Customer Admin, Vendor account owner high license_entered_grace Customer Admin, Support high offline_checkin_stale Customer Admin, Support high trial_expiring Customer Admin normal trial_expired Customer Admin normal deployment_scheduled Customer/Site Admin normal deployment_failed Customer/Site Admin, Support high rollback_completed Support, Release Manager high device_rehost_required Customer Admin, Support high entitlement_overallocation_attempt Customer Admin, Support normal

docs.title: Template rules
docs.text: Templates include customer/site/device display names, safe remediation steps and portal deep-link identifiers. They never include secrets, raw license payloads, private keys or decrypted model information.

docs.title: Delivery tracking
docs.text: Persist notification ID, event ID, recipient, channel, template version, send attempt, result and delivered timestamp. Repeated transient failures retry with backoff; permanent failures are visible to operations.

docs.title: Operational Runbook Baseline
docs.text: Runbooks are executable operational procedures for restoring service safely without requiring responders to infer architecture from source code.

docs.title: Required production runbooks
docs.text:
1. LMS API unavailable
  2. PostgreSQL degraded/unavailable
  3. signing provider unavailable
  4. artifact repository unavailable
  5. background job/outbox dead-letter backlog
  6. failed Stable rollout
  7. mass rollout pause/rollback
  8. rollback failure
  9. offline bundle rejected
  10. device stuck in REHOST_REQUIRED
  11. entitlement over-allocation/conflict
  12. renewal approved but device remains expired
  13. stale check-in spike
  14. suspected signing-key compromise
  15. tenant-isolation suspicion
  16. backup restore
  17. customer-hosted LMS recovery
  18. ERP synchronization mismatch

docs.title: Required runbook structure
docs.text: Each runbook contains: - purpose/scope - triggering alerts/symptoms - customer impact - safety/security warnings - prerequisites/permissions - diagnostic commands/portal/API checks - expected decision tree - approved remediation - retry/idempotency considerations - rollback/recovery - evidence to preserve - escalation threshold/owner - customer communication input - post-incident follow-up

docs.title: Runbook safety principles
docs.text:
• do not disable signature verification
  • do not hand-edit grants/entitlements in DB as normal remediation
  • do not move devices between tenants to fix lookup errors
  • do not delete failed deployment/audit evidence before investigation
  • do not retry non-idempotent workflows blindly
  • do not expose keys/tokens/decrypted models in tickets/chat

docs.title: Severity baseline
docs.text:
Severity Description Example Sev-1 broad critical outage/security/data exposure signing compromise, tenant breach, platform-wide license failure Sev-2 major customer/service impairment widespread deployment/renewal failure, rollback issue Sev-3 limited degradation single-customer update/rehost issue with workaround Sev-4 minor/non-urgent cosmetic/reporting issue

Severity is based on impact, security/data risk and breadth, not which module produced the error.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text: Critical runbooks are exercised in staging/tabletop/DR tests before production and after material architecture changes. Runbooks that fail during an incident are corrected as part of post-incident action.

docs.title: Support Escalation Model
docs.text: Support escalation separates safe operational recovery from engineering/security decisions. Support must not bypass licensing, signing, tenant or release controls to make a symptom disappear.

docs.title: L1 — Operations / Support
docs.text:
Handles documented runbooks: customer/site/device lookup, entitlement/allocation/grant state, renewal delivery status, offline request/response validation, deployment receipt review, standard rehost coordination and known error-code remediation.

L1 MAY retry approved operational jobs, regenerate permitted offline responses from a fresh valid request, guide package import and collect diagnostics. L1 SHALL NOT hand-edit grants, modify DB commercial state, disable signature verification or use another tenant's data to troubleshoot.

docs.title: L2 — Engineering
docs.text:
Engaged when the issue indicates a reproducible software defect, migration/update problem, unexpected state transition, capacity anomaly, integration defect, performance regression or unsupported edge/runtime condition.

L2 owns code-level diagnosis, safe fixes, regression tests and release packaging. Production data changes require approved tooling/change procedure rather than ad-hoc SQL.

docs.title: L3 — Architecture / Security / Release
docs.text: Engaged for signing/key incidents, tenant isolation suspicion, privilege/authentication failures, systemic Stable/LTS release failure, data-integrity risk, model-key compromise, cross-module design defects and emergency architecture decisions.

docs.title: Severity and target routing
docs.text: Example Typical severity Route single device package rejected with known code Sev-3/4 L1 multiple devices fail same migration Sev-2 L2 + Release broad renewal/grant issuance outage Sev-1/2 L2/L3 + Operations tenant data exposure suspicion Sev-1 Security L3 immediately signing-key compromise suspicion Sev-1 Security L3 immediately rollback also fails on production fleet Sev-1/2 L2/L3

docs.title: Escalation packet
docs.text:
Every escalation includes: - customer/site/device identifiers - request/correlation ID - stable error code - UTC timestamps + site timezone context - entitlement/allocation/grant IDs and revisions - release/model/release-set versions - deployment/installation receipt state - inventory/capacity assessment IDs where relevant - safe relevant logs - reproduction/steps already attempted - customer/business impact - whether issue is online/offline/air-gapped

Never send passwords, bearer tokens, signing/private keys, unwrapped model keys, decrypted models or unnecessary customer-sensitive payloads through ordinary support channels.

docs.title: Handoff and closure
docs.text: Receiving level explicitly accepts ownership. Resolution records root cause, remediation, affected versions, workaround, permanent fix/release, tests added and whether runbook/error catalog/documentation must change.

docs.title: Device cannot activate feature
docs.text:
1. Identify customer/site/device and request ID.
  2. Check registration state and device ownership.
  3. Check entitlement and allocation.
  4. Check latest grant issuance/delivery/acceptance state.
  5. Check commercial expiry, offline freshness and grace separately.
  6. Check device-reported rejection code.
  7. Check capacity/compatibility and installed release/model dependencies.
  8. If offline, validate request/response pairing and nonce.
  9. Apply only approved remediation; do not hand-edit grants.
  10. Record resolution/audit reference.

docs.title: Offline package rejected
docs.text:
1. Confirm package was created for the same device/request ID.
  2. Verify operator did not reuse an older response.
  3. Compare device accepted revision vs response revision.
  4. Check signature/key trust status.
  5. Check release/model compatibility.
  6. Export a fresh request if nonce/request expired or state changed.

docs.title: Deployment failed and rolled back
docs.text:
1. Confirm rollback health status.
  2. Capture installation receipt and request ID.
  3. Identify failed stage: download, verify, stage, migration, start, health check.
  4. Check disk/dependency/runtime prerequisites.
  5. Block release for broader rollout if systemic.
  6. Escalate to Release Manager when failure rate crosses rollout threshold.

docs.title: Rehost required
docs.text:
1. Confirm major hardware/key identity change.
  2. Verify customer/device ownership.
  3. Collect previous/new fingerprint evidence.
  4. Submit rehost request and required approval.
  5. Rebind identity and issue superseding grant.
  6. Retire old binding and return/reconcile allocation.

docs.title: Renewal approved but device still expired
docs.text:
1. Confirm ERP/commercial approval reached LMS.
  2. Confirm new entitlement term and grant revision exist.
  3. Check whether device has delivered/imported the new revision.
  4. For offline site, produce/import renewed response package.
  5. Confirm device accepted revision and generated receipt.

docs.title: Signing service unavailable
docs.text:
1. Stop repeated manual issuance attempts.
  2. Confirm signing gateway/provider health.
  3. Existing valid grants continue according to policy; do not bypass signature requirement.
  4. Queue issuance via outbox/retry.
  5. Escalate according to incident severity if customer activations/renewals are blocked.

docs.text: Required fields: - feature name/code and description - screenshots or approved visual assets where available - release notes/current release - product/OS/runtime compatibility - capacity preview and recommendation - current entitlement/allocation state - trial eligibility and configured duration - purchase/request-purchase action and request status - dependency/model requirements - device installation/health status

docs.title: Admin catalog view
docs.text: Required fields/actions: - feature code/name/description - supported products/OS/architecture - minimum hardware/runtime requirements - dependencies - current release and channel - trial/commercial policy - campaign configuration - release status - model associations - marketplace visibility

docs.title: Audit UX
docs.text: Every sensitive action should expose actor, timestamp, object/revision, reason, approval status and resulting state without exposing secret material.

docs.title: Role-Based Portal UX
docs.text: The portal must present role-appropriate actions while backend authorization remains authoritative.

docs.title: Vendor Super Admin
docs.text: Views: global customers, products, incidents, signing/release health, privileged audit. Actions are tightly controlled and high-risk changes require approval.

docs.title: Product Admin
docs.text: Views/actions: product/feature catalog, entitlement policy, trial campaigns, commercial configuration and approved exceptions.

docs.title: Release Manager
docs.text: Views/actions: release candidates, QA/security evidence, channels, rollout plans, deployment status, rollback and LTS designation.

docs.title: Security Approver
docs.text: Views/actions: pending maker-checker requests, signing-key changes, rehost/security overrides, VAPT/security disposition.

docs.title: Customer Admin
docs.text: Views/actions: customer sites/devices, entitlement pool, allocations, trials, purchase requests, renewals, update policy, capacity recommendations.

docs.title: Site Admin
docs.text: Views/actions: site-scoped devices, workload/capacity state, maintenance window, deployment progress and permitted site allocations.

docs.title: Support Engineer
docs.text: Views/actions: diagnostic state, request IDs, grant delivery/acceptance, offline package state, rehost/renewal workflows and safe support actions. No hidden broad commercial override.

docs.title: Read Only / Auditor
docs.text: Views: status, reports and audit history without mutation.

docs.title: Critical UX rules
docs.text:
• Always distinguish registration, license, capacity and install/health status.
  • Always distinguish issued, delivered and accepted grants.
  • Show why an action is blocked with safe error/reason codes.
  • Offline export/import screens display request ID, target device, expiry, package version and reconciliation status.
  • Capacity screens show purchased rights separately from selected active configuration and recommendation.
  • Privileged actions show approval state and second-approver requirement before execution.

docs.title: Product & Scope
docs.text: LMS is the enterprise control plane for customer/device identity, commercial rights, capacity feasibility, feature discovery/delivery and edge lifecycle across connected, customer-hosted and air-gapped AI deployments.

docs.title: Product problem
docs.text: Without a common control plane, every product tends to invent its own customer registry, licensing, trials, feature delivery, renewal and offline process. That makes enterprise deployment difficult to monetize, support and audit. LMS standardizes those concerns while leaving product analytics execution on the edge.

docs.title: Primary outcomes
docs.text:
• onboard customers/sites/devices once
  • represent commercial rights generically
  • allocate pooled rights without over-allocation
  • issue device-bound signed authorization
  • plan and validate real hardware capacity
  • expose marketplace/trial/purchase workflows
  • safely deliver application/model updates online/offline
  • renew/revoke/rehost/transfer with auditable lifecycle state
  • support SaaS and customer-hosted operations from one codebase

docs.title: Actors
docs.text: Actor Primary responsibility Vendor Super Admin global platform/customer administration; high-risk governance Product Admin product/feature/commercial/trial policy Release Manager release promotion, rollout and rollback Security Approver security-sensitive approvals/key/trust actions Developer non-production development artifacts/code Support Engineer diagnostics/runbook/recovery within scoped permission Customer Admin customer sites/devices/allocations/trials/renewals/policies Site Admin site-scoped operations/workload/update visibility Read-Only Auditor audit/compliance visibility Edge Device / Server cryptographic identity, local verification/capacity/update/runtime

docs.title: Ownership topology
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    C[Customer / Tenant] --> S1[Site A]
    C --> S2[Site B]
    C --> D[Owned Device / Server]
    D --> A1[Device-Site Assignment]
    A1 --> S1
    A1 --> S2

A device has one commercial customer owner at a time but may serve multiple sites through explicit assignments.

docs.title: LMS owns
docs.text: customer/site/device operational topology, entitlements, allocations, grants, trials, capacity evidence, marketplace state, release/model metadata, deployments, renewals/check-ins, offline exchange, notifications and audit.

docs.title: Edge owns
docs.text: device private identity, actual runtime workload, local authorization enforcement, local capacity authority, install/health/rollback and signed receipts.

docs.title: ERP owns when integrated
docs.text: orders, invoices/payment and contract financial truth. LMS imports approved commercial state but is not an accounting system.

docs.title: Critical separations
docs.text: Registered != Licensed != Capacity Validated != Installed/Healthy and Issued != Delivered != Accepted. These distinctions are visible in APIs, portal and support workflows.

docs.title: Product non-goals
docs.text: See Goals & Non-Goals. The platform does not promise software-only tamper-proof operation on a hostile root-owned device, does not require continuous internet, does not use telemetry as paid-license renewal, and does not silently reduce purchased rights because hardware is insufficient.

docs.title: Normative sources
docs.text: System Design Requirements define testable SHALL requirements. ADRs explain durable architecture choices. Consolidated Business Rules define cross-domain commercial/lifecycle invariants.

docs.title: Consolidated Business Rules
docs.text: This page is the normative cross-domain business-rule checklist for LMS. More detailed pages remain authoritative for implementation specifics.

docs.title: Licensing and entitlement
docs.text:
• Registration, commercial licensing and capacity validation are separate states.
  • Entitlement = what the customer owns; allocation = distribution of pooled rights; grant = device-bound signed executable authorization.
  • Customer pooled quantity must never be over-allocated.
  • Reallocation creates superseding grants and must not allow old/new quantities to remain simultaneously usable indefinitely.
  • Subscription and perpetual base licenses are supported.
  • Subscription add-ons co-terminate with the base by default; explicitly independent add-ons may have their own term.
  • A perpetual base may carry subscription add-ons.
  • Dependent add-ons become dormant when the required base is inactive.
  • Commercial expiry, offline authorization freshness and grace are three independent clocks.
  • Successful check-in never extends commercial expiry.
  • Payment/renewal approval alone does not renew an offline device until it receives and accepts the new signed grant revision.

docs.title: Trials
docs.text:
• Default trial duration is 7 days and is policy-configurable.
  • Trial starts on first successful feature activation, not on request, issuance or package import.
  • Baseline eligibility is one trial per customer entitlement + feature, unless an auditable admin/campaign override permits another trial.
  • A trial is a signed time-limited grant; globally reusable trial licenses are prohibited.

docs.title: Device lifecycle
docs.text:
• Device identity is cryptographic key + versioned weighted hardware fingerprint; MAC is evidence only.
  • Minor hardware changes trigger re-evaluation and normally continue.
  • Major identity changes enter REHOST_REQUIRED; they do not silently destroy or transfer licenses.
  • Decommission/replacement returns eligible allocation to the entitlement pool after approval/reconciliation.
  • Device transfer is request/approval/audit driven; ownership is never silently overwritten.
  • Air-gapped revocation becomes effective only after signed state is imported or existing offline authorization expires.

docs.title: Capacity
docs.text:
• Central capacity assessment is advisory/pre-assessment; local capacity check is authoritative for actual activation.
  • Commercial rights are never silently reduced because hardware is insufficient.
  • Capacity engine recommends alternatives; an operator/customer chooses the allowed configuration.

docs.title: Marketplace and OTA
docs.text:
• Marketplace discovery/trial/purchase does not itself authorize execution.
  • A feature activates only when compatible, licensed, installed, healthy and capacity-validated.
  • Automatic production updates consume Stable by default.
  • LTS deployment is explicitly company-controlled.
  • Normal site releases must automate migration, health-check and rollback; no manual migration step.
  • Models are independently versioned, encrypted, signed and inventory-aware.
  • Offline bundles should contain only missing/required artifacts where possible.

docs.title: Governance
docs.text:
• High-risk actions use maker-checker approval.
  • Audit retention baseline is configurable 1–3 years.
  • Portal + email are initial notification channels; webhook delivery remains extensible.
  • LMS is not an accounting system; ERP integration is separate.
